AlertResultMsg.description: The answer to `alert_test`, when the command has ended or run out of its 20 s.

ok.description: the command ended with exit code 0

outcome.description: how it ended, which the page says in its words: `ran` it worked; `exit` it ended with the exit code `status`; `timeout` it did not end within `seconds` and was killed; `no_start` it could not start (the log says why)

seconds.description: how long a run may take, in seconds

line.description: for `exit`, the first line the command wrote to stderr, its own words (`no display`); empty otherwise

AlertResultMsg.title: AlertResultMessage

AlertTest.description:
Runs the alert command as it is saved in the settings (`messages/alert_command`), exactly as for a message to us (the same shell, the same environment, the 20 s limit) with a made-up message: `NEOAPRS_FROM`
is `NEOAPRS`, `NEOAPRS_TEXT` is `This is a test of the NeoAPRS alert`, `NEOAPRS_AT` is now and `NEOAPRS_MSG_ID` is empty. `messages/alert` is not asked: a test is explicit. Waits for the command and answers the page
that asked with `alert_result`, or with an `error` when the command is empty (`no alert command`). A page of another device is refused with `setting.local_only`.
AlertTest.title: AlertTestCommand

AlertWhen.description:
When the operator is told about a station: any of the three, each once for each time it happens (it is not told again for every packet), by the message `station_alert` to every page and by the alert command of
the settings (`messages/alert`, `messages/alert_command`), as a message to us is.

on_air.description: a packet of the station is heard after it was silent for 30 minutes or more, or for the first time; a packet over the internet counts while `igate/enabled` is on

within_km.description: its position comes from farther to this many km from us or nearer (it is outside again only some way beyond: a tenth more, at least 0.5 km); null if the distance is not watched. A station that is that near already when the alert is set is not told until it has been outside

direct.description: a packet of it is heard direct (no digipeater) after none was for 30 minutes or more

AlertWhen.title: AlertWhen

AlohaCircle.description: The ALOHA circle of one radio: the distance within which the stations that radio heard would fill its 1200 baud channel (WB4APR's method, worked out again every minute).

radio.description: the radio's id

km.description: the radius round our position, in km to a tenth

AlohaCircle.title: AlohaCircle

AreaValues.description: An area object (the symbol `\l`): its shape and colour, and how far down and to the right of the object's position it reaches.

shape.description: the shape, which the page says in its words

colour.description: the colour, which the page says in its words; `unknown` for a number the specification has no colour for

AreaValues.title: AreaValues

AskQru.description:
Asks the stations near us for local info (repeaters, events, places): one message to the addressee `QRU` (the services/qruask.py of the daemon), whose `text` is `INFO` (which groups are served near
us?), `NEXT` (the next objects of the group asked for last) or a group of 1 to 8 upper-case letters and digits (`RP70`), with a distance in kilometres, 1 to 20000, after it (`INFO 250`). A request to QRU is a
broadcast: it is sent once, with no message id, is not kept as a message and is not sent again; it goes by `path` when one is given (digipeater calls or aliases separated by commas, checked as a radio's
path is, or `DIRECT` for none), else by the path of messages to the station QRU (its own path, else the radio's), with RFONLY after it unless `rf_only` is false: by radio only. With no `radio` it goes
once on each radio of Local info's Send on (the radios whose `radio/<id>/local_info` is ticked; with one radio that can send, that one) that takes
frames now; with `radio`, on that radio alone. The answers come as messages to us (they are rows of the topic `messages` like any message) and as the topic `qru`; the objects arrive as objects. All or
nothing: answered with an `error`, and nothing is sent on any radio, when the text is none, the station is RX only or no call is set (`transmit.off`, or the interlock's reason), there is no radio
(`radio.none`) or none takes frames now, a request to QRU went on one of its radios less than 60 seconds ago with the same text or any less than 10 seconds ago (`qru.too_soon`, with the `seconds` that
are left, the longest), or the path is no path or too long with RFONLY (`path.*`, `call.*`).

path.description: the path the request goes by; left out (or null, or empty) the path of messages to QRU

rf_only.description: RFONLY after the path; left out it is true. The page no longer sends it (the request always goes with RFONLY); a page of an older build may

radio.description: the one radio the request goes on, its id: the radio a server answered on (`QruServer.radio`), for a request of a group it listed or one asked again; left out: the radios of Local info's Send on. Refused with `radio.unknown` for a radio that is none, `radio.off` for one that is off, `radio.receive_only` for one that only receives and `radio.not_connected` for one that is not connected

AskQru.title: AskQruCommand

AskStatus.description: Answered with `status` at once (the daemon also sends one every 10 s).
AskStatus.title: AskStatusCommand

AttemptRow.description: One transmission of a message of ours and what came back of it.

hops.description: the digipeaters of the path the attempt went by, in order; empty for a direct path

internet.description: the call of the iGate that put a copy of the message back on the air as a third-party packet, when one was heard for this attempt; null otherwise

acked.description: the acknowledgement was heard after this attempt and before the next one: the attempt the ack answers

radio_id.description: the radio the attempt went out on, its id (a row of the topic `radios`); null for an attempt kept before the radio was

AttemptRow.title: AttemptRow

BeaconNow.description:
Sends our position packet now, with the settings as they are (the same packet as the timer's), and the next one is an interval later. It goes out through the TNC, so it is not answered:
it arrives as the new `packets` row with direction `out`, and `status` follows with the time of the beacon. Answered with an `error` when it could not be sent: the TNC is not connected, or
the settings make no frame.
BeaconNow.title: BeaconNowCommand

BulletinDelete.description:
Removes an entry from the message board, from the database and from every page: its row is a `del` of the topic `bulletins`. The same bulletin heard again afterwards is a new entry (heard once). Answered by
the `del`, or by an `error` (no such entry).

sender.description: the call that sent it, as the row has it

slot.description: the addressee as the row has it: `BLN1`, `BLNA`, `BLN3HAMS`, `QST`

BulletinDelete.title: BulletinDeleteCommand

BulletinPost.description:
Posts a bulletin, an announcement or a group bulletin of ours in the lowest free slot of its kind: `BLN0`..`BLN9` for a bulletin, `BLNA`..`BLNZ` for an announcement, `BLN0`..`BLN9` and the group for a
group bulletin (`BLN0HAMS`); a slot is free while no post of ours is in it, an ended one included. Nothing of ours is replaced: with every slot of the kind (of the group) taken it is refused (`bulletin.taken`),
and so it is with 36 posts of ours (`bulletin.full`). `text` is at most 67 characters of printable ASCII without `|`, `~` and `{`. It is sent at once and then on the schedule of the specification (a bulletin
a few times early and every 20 minutes, an announcement every hour) for `hours`. Nothing is sent while the call is not set. Answered by the `set` of its row in `own_bulletins`, or by an `error` that names the
reason.

group.description: the group of a group bulletin, 1 to 5 letters and digits (written in capitals); ignored for the other kinds

hours.description: how long it is sent after its first packet, in hours: 1, 2, 4, 8 or 12 for a bulletin and a group bulletin, 24, 72 or 168 for an announcement; left out: `status.new_bulletin_hours` of its kind

radios.description: the radios it goes out on, their ids; left out: `status.new_bulletin_radios`

BulletinPost.title: BulletinPostCommand

BulletinRow.description:
One bulletin, announcement, group bulletin or group message on the board: what a station sent to `BLN0`..`BLN9`, `BLNA`..`BLNZ`, `BLN3HAMS` (a number or letter and a group of up to five characters) or `ALL`, `CQ`
or `QST`. None of them is a conversation and none is acked. The rows are the values of the topic `bulletins`, keyed by `sender/slot` (`OH2XYZ/BLN1`): the board holds one row for each sender and slot, a sender
sending the slot again replaces the text. A bulletin that is new or heard again is a `set` of its row, one that is deleted (`bulletin_delete`) a `del`. Nothing ages out: an
entry stays on the board until it is deleted.

sender.description: the call that sent it (for a third-party packet the call inside it)

group.description: the group of a group bulletin (`HAMS` of `BLN3HAMS`); empty for any other

kind.description: `announcement` is `BLNA`..`BLNZ`, `bulletin` is `BLN0`..`BLN9`, `group` is a group bulletin or a message to `ALL`, `CQ` or `QST`, `nws` is a weather service bulletin (`NWS-xxxxx`, `SKY...`, `CWA...`)

first_heard.description: when this text was first heard; a sender that changes the text starts again

times_heard.description: how often this text was heard (the copies of one transmission that came by different digipeaters within 10 seconds are one)

BulletinRow.title: BulletinRow

BulletinUnpost.description: Deletes a bulletin of ours: it is not sent again and leaves the board. Answered by the `del` of its row in `own_bulletins`, or by an `error` (no such bulletin of ours).
BulletinUnpost.title: BulletinUnpostCommand

CardLevelsRow.description: The radio's sound card's own levels (the radio's `tx_card` and `rx_card` set them): a slider is drawn only where the card has the control, at the card's level.

tx.description: the card's playback level in percent, what the radio is given to transmit (ALSA's Speaker, PCM or Master control; the playing device's master volume on Windows); null where the card has no such control, the radio has no sound card or its card was never read

rx.description: the card's capture level in percent, what it takes from the radio (ALSA's Capture or Mic control; the recording device's master volume on Windows); null as `tx`

read.description: the levels are the card's: its card was read in this run of the daemon, or there is nothing to wait for (this system has no mixer, the radio has no sound card of its own); false while an enabled radio's card was not read yet, and for a radio that is off and was never read in this run. While false the page draws neither the slider nor the modem's - and +, so that the row has one shape from its first paint

CardLevelsRow.title: CardLevelsRow

ChannelHours.description: The packets one radio, or the internet, heard in each hour.

radio.description: the radio that heard them, its id (a row of the topic `radios`, a removed one too); null for the internet

counts.description: the packets heard in each hour from the message's `start`, the oldest first, `hours` of them (an hour with none is 0)

ChannelHours.title: ChannelHours

ChatFreshMsg.description: Lines of others came into the chat that were not seen before (newer than the newest this installation had seen, a restart too): told to every page that is open, once for the lines of one reading, and only while `messages/chat_alert` is on. The page alerts as for a message to us (the sound, the notification, the browser tab, as its own choice says).

call.description: who said the newest

ChatFreshMsg.title: ChatFreshMessage

ChatLineRow.description: A line of the chat, checked again by the daemon: one line of text of at most 200 characters, without control or invisible characters, never empty. The page shows it as text, never as markup.

id.description: the server's id of the line, which grows by one with each line said

at.description: when the server took it, by the server's clock

call.description: the call that said it, upper case without an SSID of 0 (`OH2GBA`, `OH2GBA-7`)

ours.description: this installation said it, or it is under our call: it never notifies

ChatLineRow.title: ChatLineRow

ChatSay.description:
Says a line in the chat of the HF tests tab: the daemon posts it to the project's server with our call (the setting `station/call`, as the board has it) and this installation's token, over the Internet and never by radio. Cleaned as the server cleans it (white space
becomes single spaces, control and invisible characters go, at most 200 characters). Answered by the topic `chat_lines`, which then has it with `ours` true. An `error` when no call is set (the interlock's reason; RX only does not matter), too many lines were said from here
in the last minute (`chat.rate`), the chat takes no lines now (`chat.closed`; the topic `chat` then says `closed`), the server did not take the line (`chat.refused`), or the project's server could not be reached or would not take it (`chat.unreachable`).

text.description: the line; not empty once cleaned

ChatSay.title: ChatSayCommand

ChatState.description: Where the chat stands. The value of the topic `chat`, told whole as it changes.

state.description: `ok`: the chat was read (or has not been tried yet), and a line may be said. `offline`: the project's server could not be read; `chat_lines` are the last ones known. `off`: the check is off (`NEOAPRS_UPDATE_CHECK=0`): nothing is read or said, `chat_lines` is empty. `closed`: the chat takes no lines now (closed by the project, or for this call); the lines are still shown

ChatState.title: ChatState

CheckUpdate.description: Asks the version page now, the question of the daily update check; the daily schedule is left as it was. Answered with `update_result` and then a `status` (with the newer version, if there is one) to the page that asked.
CheckUpdate.title: CheckUpdateCommand

ClearStationPath.description:
Takes a station's own path away, so that it has the path of the setting `beacon/path` again (a station without one is no error). Answered by the `set` of its entry in `station_prefs` with a null `path`
(or the `del` of the entry when it was not RF only either), or by an `error`.

radio.description: the radio whose path for the station is taken away, its id; left out: radio 1

ClearStationPath.title: ClearStationPathCommand

ConfigValues.description:
The settings: each key of the station's settings (`station/call`, `beacon/interval_min`, ...) with its value as text, the way the daemon writes it, and the defaults beside them. The value of the topic
`config`, told again after every save, though nothing differs.

values.description: the settings in force, key to text; every key is there (the keys of `CONFIG_KEYS`: the station's settings, and `serial/last_port`, the port radio 1's search found last, which the page shows and does not set)

defaults.description: the same keys with their defaults, for a form's reset

radio_values.description: the radios' own settings in force, `radio/<id>/<key>` to text, every field of its kind for each radio that is not removed (the fields of `RADIO_TYPES`), and the station's settings of the radios (`email/radio`, the id of the radio chosen for email, empty for none chosen: the radio in force is `status.email_radio`): what `set_config` takes beside `values`; kept apart from `values`, whose form shows none of them; and both keys of every two radios that are not removed and may form a pair (both transmit, both Dummy or both real), enabled or not: `pair/<low>/<high>/enabled` (`true` or `false`) and `pair/<low>/<high>/ssid` (1 to 15, the SSID of the pair's call on the station's base call; empty while none is chosen, and a pair switched on is given the highest free one), by the radios' ids, low first

radio_defaults.description: the same keys with their defaults (the field's of the radio's kind; a pair's `false` and empty)

urls.description: where another device opens the page while `web/network` is on (this computer's address on the network and its name there, with the port); empty while it is off (with `https` on, the https addresses)

https.description: the secure connection: whether it is served, its port, the fingerprint of the authority's certificate (which `GET /neoaprs-ca.crt` downloads), and why not when it could not start

ConfigValues.title: ConfigValues

ConversationDelete.description:
Removes the whole conversation with a station: every message we sent to it and every one it sent to us (not the messages it was only overheard sending to others), from the database in one write, from
the daemon and from every page: each message's row is a `del` of the topic `messages`. A message that is still being sent is cancelled first. The path and the timeout of the station stay. Answered by the
`del`s, or by an `error` (the call is none, or there is no message with that station).
ConversationDelete.title: ConversationDeleteCommand

DecodedItem.description: An item report: like an object, without a time.
DecodedItem.title: DecodedItem

DecodedMessage.description: A text message; an ack has `ack_id` and no text, a reject `rej_id`.
DecodedMessage.title: DecodedMessage

DecodedObject.description: An object report: a thing (a storm, an event) that a station puts on the map.

alive.description: false when the report kills the object

anyOf.description: UTC, ISO 8601 with a Z, with fractions of a second

DecodedObject.title: DecodedObject

DecodedOther.description: A data type that is recognised but not (fully) decoded: a positionless weather report is decoded (`weather`, `timestamp`), the station capabilities and an Agrelo DF report are read into `items`.

kind.description: what kind of packet it is: one of these words, which the page says in its words; `telemetry` is one that is not a report, `unknown` a data type the parser does not know

weather.description: the observation of a positionless weather report (`_`); null for anything else

items.description: `capabilities`: the items of the list by token (`IGATE`, `MSG_CNT`...), the value empty for a token alone; `agrelo-df`: `bearing` and `quality`; null for anything else

anyOf.description: UTC, ISO 8601 with a Z, with fractions of a second

timestamp.description: the time of a positionless weather report (its MMDDhhmm, resolved to the latest such time that is not in the future)

DecodedOther.title: DecodedOther

anyOf.description: UTC, ISO 8601 with a Z, with fractions of a second

timestamp.description: the time the packet itself carries, when it has one

ambiguity.description: how many digits of the position were blanked out, 0 to 4

weather.description: the weather a station with the weather symbol (`_`) sent after its position; the rest of the text is the `comment`

extensions.description: the PHG, RNG, DFS, DF bearing or area data after the symbol of an uncompressed position; null when there was none

timestamp_local.description: the `timestamp` was sent in the sender's local time (`/`): it is the time as it was sent, not UTC

locator.description: the Maidenhead locator in the status text of a Mic-E packet; null for any other position

telemetry.description: the base-91 telemetry `|ss11|` the comment carried (APRS 1.2), taken out of the `comment`; null when there was none

frequency.description: the local information the comment began with (`145.775MHz T100 -060 R40k`), or the name of a frequency object with the fields of its comment, taken out of the `comment`; null when there was none

storm.description: the storm data the comment of a position with the symbol `@` began with (`/HC/150^200/0980>090&030%040`), taken out of the `comment`; null when there was none

sign.description: the characters of a signpost (symbol `\m`): `55` for a comment that began `{55}`, taken out of the `comment`; null for any other position

text.description: the status text; after the locator when there is one

anyOf.description: UTC, ISO 8601 with a Z, with fractions of a second

locator.description: a Maidenhead locator with a symbol at the start of the report (a report that has one has no timestamp)

frequency.description: the frequency the text began with (`>145.775MHz T100`), taken out of the `text`; null when there was none

DecodedTelemetry.description: A telemetry report (`T#005,199,000,255,073,123,01101001`). The definitions of the channels are messages of the station, applied by the daemon: see `telemetry` of the station.

sequence.description: the sequence number; null for the `MIC` of a Mic-E unit

analog.description: the analog values as sent, 1 to 5 (APRS 1.2: any width, signed, with a decimal point)

bits.description: the digital values as a text of 0 and 1, B1 first: up to eight, empty when there were none

DecodedTelemetry.title: DecodedTelemetry

DecodedUndecoded.description: A field that should have decoded and did not.

code.description: what could not be read, which the page says in its words (the log has the parser's own): `empty` the information field is empty; `position` a position (of an object or an item too); `mice` a Mic-E position; `message` a message; `nmea` a GPS sentence; `damaged` anything else, and a packet kept before there was a code

DecodedUndecoded.title: DecodedUndecoded

DecodedWeather.description: The weather fields of a weather station's position or of a positionless weather report, in metric units; null where the report did not have the field.

rain_counter.description: the raw rain counter, as the station counts it

raw.description: the weather fields as they were sent

DecodedWeather.title: DecodedWeather

key.description: the key of an item of a keyed topic: a station's call, a packet's id as text

DfBearingValues.description: The bearing and quality of a DF report (`/270/729` after the course and speed).

hits.description: 0 nothing, 1 to 8 the share of the possible samples that hit, 9 a manual report

range_km.description: the length the line is drawn to

DfBearingValues.title: DfBearingValues

DfsValues.description: The strength of a signal heard by a direction finder (`DFS2360`) with the height, gain and directivity of its antenna.

strength.description: 0 to 9; 0 is where the signal is not heard

DfsValues.title: DfsValues

Error.description:
A command that could not be done. A frame the daemon could not understand is answered the same way, naming the command, the field and the problem; nothing was changed. A page goes by `cmd`, `key`
and `code` (with the sentence of `why` for a refusal that passes another's on); `text` is the English sentence for the log, which the page never shows: a code it has no sentence for is said with its plain
words of a failure.

cmd.description: the command it answers; empty for a frame that was no command (not JSON, not an object, no `cmd`, an unknown one)

key.description: the setting it is about (`set_config`), a key of `CONFIG_KEYS`; null for any other error

code.description: a stable word for what is wrong, such as `setting.range`, `call.ssid` or `message.too_long`; `failed` for one the operator can do nothing about; `other` for an error that has no code

params.description: the values the sentence is made of, by name, such as `value`, `min` and `max` of `setting.range`, and `why`, the code of the reason, for a refusal that passes another's on (`status.not_sent`, `beacon.not_sent`, `transmit.call`); empty when there are none

text.description: what could not be done and why, in a sentence in English: the command, then the setting if there is one, then the reason (`set_config: station/lat: 95 is not between -90 and 90`)

id.description: the `id` of the request this answers, when the command carried one (only `set_config` does: the `id` of another command is a radio's, a message's or a packet's number and is never echoed); the field is left out otherwise

Error.title: ErrorMessage

ExtensionValues.description: The data extensions after the symbol of an uncompressed position (taken off the comment); null for what the position did not have.
ExtensionValues.title: ExtensionValues

FindRadio.description:
Find my radio: tries the serial ports and the paired Bluetooth devices that the search for the radio looks at (not a KISS TCP address), one after the other and each at the usual speeds, until a TNC answers in KISS or can be
put into KISS the way a TNC profile does. The radio's own line is closed while it runs and opened again after it. It writes nothing but a carriage return and, to a TNC that answers with text, the steps of the TNC profiles that
put it into KISS; nothing is sent to the air. Told to the page that asked with `radio_search` messages (`trying` before each try, then `found` or `cancelled`); the page puts the answer in the settings. An `error` when a search is running
(`radio.busy`), when there is no port to try (`radio.no_ports`), when none answered (`radio.not_found`), for a `radio` that is none (`radio.unknown`) and for one of a type that has no serial line (`radio.no_line`). Only that radio's line is
let go (radio 1's when `radio` is left out), the ports another radio or the GPS receiver holds are passed over, and the messages name it.

radio.description: the radio the search is for (its id); left out: radio 1, the packet radio of before

FindRadio.title: FindRadioCommand

FindRadioCancel.description:
Ends the search of `find_radio`; the page that asked is told `cancelled`. An `error` (`radio.not_running`) when none is running. One search runs at a time, so `radio` changes nothing: it is taken so that the page names the radio
in every command of its box.

radio.description: the radio whose search is ended; left out: the one running

FindRadioCancel.title: FindRadioCancelCommand

ForgetAllStations.description:
A fresh start for what was heard: removes every station and every packet heard (and the weather of the stations), in the daemon and in its database. The station we are, the objects and bulletins we send, the messages, the
settings and the maps stay, and so do the packets we sent. Answered by the stations' topic told whole, or by an `error`.
ForgetAllStations.title: ForgetAllStationsCommand

ForgetStation.description: Removes a station from the station book (and its cache in the database) until it is heard again. Not our own station. Answered by the `del` of the row, or by an `error`.
ForgetStation.title: ForgetStationCommand

ForgetStationKey.description:
Takes a station's key away (the topic `station_keys`): the first key a station announces is kept, and a later announcement of a different key is not taken until the old one is forgotten. Answered by the `del` of the
station's entry, or by an `error` (`lock.no_key` when there is none).
ForgetStationKey.title: ForgetStationKeyCommand

Frequencies.description:
The page shows the station's suggested frequencies (the box of a radio whose type can show them, the HF tests tab): the daemon asks the project's server for them again, unless it asked less than 15 minutes ago or the
update check is off (`NEOAPRS_UPDATE_CHECK=0`). The suggested dials are the project's, not a radio's: one list for the station. Nothing is answered; the topic `skeds` and each Mercury radio's `modem` have the list
when it changes.
Frequencies.title: FrequenciesCommand

FrequencyRow.description: A frequency the project suggests for the HF radio.

dial.description: the dial with its mode, `7.0541 MHz USB`

FrequencyRow.title: FrequencyRow

FrequencyValues.description: A frequency to call on, from the local information at the start of a comment, a status text or the name of a frequency object (`145.775MHz T100 -060 R40k`); null where the text did not say.

tone_hz.description: the CTCSS tone of `Tnnn` or `Cnnn`, whole hertz (the tenths are dropped: 107 is 107.2)

tone_both.description: `Cnnn`: the tone is needed to receive as well

tone_off.description: `Toff`: no tone and no DCS code

dcs.description: the DCS code of `Dnnn`, three digits as sent

tone_burst.description: `1750`: a 1750 Hz tone burst opens the repeater

narrow.description: the first letter of the tone field was lower case: narrow modulation

offset_khz.description: the offset from the transmit frequency in kHz (`-060` is -600); 0 is simplex; null when the standard offset is meant

FrequencyValues.title: FrequencyValues

GeneralAsked.description: A general query sent from here: one press, on one or more radios.

query.description: the information field it went with, `?APRS?`, `?IGATE?` or `?WX?`

radios.description: the radios it went on, their ids, in the order of their boxes; what any of them heard is counted in `new`

path.description: the path it went by on the radios that carry one, `RFONLY` last when it was RF only; empty for no digipeaters; null when none was given and those radios' own paths differ

until.description: when the counting of `new` ends, two minutes after it was sent

new.description: the calls of the stations heard on one of its radios (not as a third-party packet, not from the internet) between the query and `until` that this radio had not heard in the ten minutes before it, in the order they were heard, each once whatever number of radios heard it: most are answers, but a station cannot be told to answer, so this is no more than who spoke after a quiet spell

GeneralAsked.title: GeneralAsked

GeneralQuery.description:
Asks the stations in radio range a general query of APRS 1.0.1 (the services/generalask.py of the daemon): one frame from our call to our tocall whose information field is exactly `?APRS?` (`kind`
`aprs`: who is around? the stations answer with their positions), `?IGATE?` (`igate`: the iGates answer with their capabilities) or `?WX?` (`wx`: the weather stations answer with their weather). It goes
once on each radio of asking around's Send on (the radios whose `radio/<id>/ask` is ticked; with one radio that can send, that one) that takes
frames now, by `path` (digipeater calls or aliases separated by commas, `OH2RDK-7,OH2RCH-2` or `WIDE1-1,WIDE2-1`, checked as a radio's path is, or `DIRECT` for none; null or empty is each radio's own
path, and a radio that carries no path goes without one) with `RFONLY` after it when `rf_only`. The answers are ordinary packets (rows of `stations` and `packets`); the topic `general` tells the query and the
stations heard after it. All or nothing: answered with an `error`, and nothing is sent on any radio, when the station is RX only or no call is set (`transmit.off`, or the interlock's reason), there is no
radio (`radio.none`) or none of them takes frames now, the path is no path (`path.*`, `call.*`) or is too long with RFONLY (`path.too_long_rf_only`), or the query of that kind went on one of those
radios less than 60 seconds ago (`general.too_soon`, with the `seconds` that are left, the longest).

rf_only.description: RFONLY after the path; left out it is true. The page no longer sends it (the request always goes with RFONLY); a page of an older build may

GeneralQuery.title: GeneralQueryCommand

GeneralSent.description: The last query of a kind on one radio.

radio.description: the radio, its id

at.description: when it went on that radio

GeneralSent.title: GeneralSent

GeneralState.description: The general queries sent from here: the last one of each kind. Forgotten when the daemon stops. Told whole as it changes.

asked.description: the last query of each kind, the oldest first; empty before one

by_radio.description: when the last query of each kind went on each radio, the oldest first: the wait before the next of a kind is each radio's, and a query waits for every radio it would go on (`general.too_soon`)

GeneralState.title: GeneralState

GpsState.description: The GPS receiver and what the beacon does with it: the latest fix, whether it can be used, and the beacon of a moving station. Told whole as it changes, at most once a second.

source.description: `gps/source` as in force: where the fixes come from

state.description: `off`: no source is set; `connecting`: the line to gpsd or the receiver is not up and no fix has come; `no_fix`: it is up and the receiver has no fix; `fix`: the latest fix is fresh; `stale`: the latest fix is older than 120 seconds and is not used (a mobile beacon sends nothing on it)

reason.description: why there is no fix to use, as a code the page says in its words, where `state` does not say it already (the log has the feed's own words): `no_port` no port of the receiver is set; `no_address` no address of gpsd is set; `held` the receiver's port is held by a radio; `no_answer` the receiver or gpsd does not answer, or its line was lost; empty for `off`, `fix`, `stale` and a plain wait or no fix

lat.description: the latest fix, degrees north; null before the first fix of the source (a stale fix is still told, with its `fix_at`)

altitude_m.description: metres above mean sea level; null when the fix has none

speed_kmh.description: kilometres per hour; null when the fix has none

course_deg.description: degrees from north, 0 to 359; null when the fix has none

satellites.description: the satellites used for the fix; null when the source does not say

fix_at.description: when the latest fix was received, by the daemon's clock

mobile.description: `gps/source` is not `off`: the beacon follows the GPS. With no fresh fix nothing is sent at all (never the home position), which `state` and `reason` say

next_beacon_at.description: when the next beacon by time is due, for the speed of the latest fix (a turn sends one sooner); null unless the beacon is mobile and has a fresh fix and has sent its first

last_beacon_reason.description: why the latest mobile beacon of this run went out: `start` (the first fix), `time`, `turn` (a corner), `request` (Beacon now); empty before the first

last_beacon_at.description: when it went out; null before the first

GpsState.title: GpsState

HeardOn.description: What one radio heard of a station.

count.description: how many of the packets of the air (`rf`, `rf-gated` and `dummy` alike) came on the radio

last_at.description: when the latest of them did; null when that is not known

HeardOn.title: HeardOn

Hello.description: The first message of a connection; `status` and the `state` of every topic follow it at once, so a page need not ask for them.

protocol.description: the version of these messages: a page built for another one loads itself again, and when that does not help it does not run (it shows a notice and keeps the socket closed)

version.description: the version of the daemon, which the page shows (Settings → Update check); the page has no version of its own and does not compare this one

page.description: the build of the page this daemon serves, the name of its main script (`index-<hash>.js` of assets/); the daemon serves the page it took when it started, so this is the build a browser gets from it. A page of another build loads itself again, once for each build, and shows a notice when that does not help; empty when the daemon has no built page

install.description: how this daemon was installed, for the steps of an update

local.description: whether this page is on the computer the daemon runs on (the loopback, with a request addressed to it): only such a page changes the settings that name a program or an address the daemon runs or fetches from (messages/alert_command, update/url, map/source, web/allowed_hosts) and runs the alert's Test; a page of another device does not show them

topics.description: the topics the page is following from the start: all of them (a page may `unsubscribe` from one)

Hello.title: HelloMessage

HopRow.description: One digipeater of the path an attempt went by, and whether a copy of our own message was heard back with that hop used.

call.description: the digipeater as the path named it (`OH2RCH-2`, or an alias such as `WIDE1-1`); once heard, the call that did it, which replaces an alias

heard.description: a copy was heard by radio with this hop's has-been-repeated bit set (or a later hop's: a hop works the first unused address)

heard_at.description: when the first copy that showed the hop was heard (by radio if there was one, else over the internet); null when it was not heard

by_internet.description: a copy gated back by an iGate as a third-party packet showed the hop used; with `heard` false the hop is known only that way

HopRow.title: HopRow

HttpsState.description: The secure connection (`web/https`) as the daemon has it.

on.description: the page is served over https right now (`web/https` and `web/network` are on, and it started)

port.description: the https port; 0 while it is not served

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of NeoAPRS's certificate authority, `AB:CD:...`, for a person to compare with what the device shows when the certificate is installed; empty while it is not served

reason.description: why the secure connection could not start or go on, when it was asked for, as a code the page says in its words (the log has the details): `no_library` this installation cannot make it; `clock` the clock of this computer is not set; `certificates` the certificates could not be made, read or loaded; `no_port` no port after the page's own was free for it; empty otherwise

HttpsState.title: HttpsState

IgateLook.description:
With `on`, this page shows the lines that Send what I hear has put on APRS-IS (the Internet box of the settings is open, `igate/gate` is on and the page is in front): it is sent `igate_sent` with the kept lines at once and then each line as it is
sent. With `on` false, or when the page closes, no more. Never refused.
IgateLook.title: IgateLookCommand

IgateSentLine.description: A line that was put on APRS-IS.

radio.description: the radio that heard the packet; null for our own position

line.description: the line as it went to the server, after the gating rules (the TNC2 text): other stations' data, shown as text only

IgateSentLine.title: IgateSentLine

IgateSentMsg.description: The lines put on APRS-IS, to a page that looks (`igate_look`): `whole` true replaces the page's list with `lines` (the newest 200 since the daemon started, oldest first, as the page opened the box), false adds `lines` (one line as it is sent) to its end.
IgateSentMsg.title: IgateSentMessage

IgateState.description:
The login to APRS-IS (neoaprs/services/igate.py): it shows the internet's stations (`igate/enabled`), puts what the radios hear on APRS-IS (`igate/gate`, the iGate), or both, and nothing from APRS-IS is
ever sent on the air. Whether it is connected, to which server, and what it has done since the daemon started. Told whole as it changes, at most once a second.

show_gated.description: `igate/show_gated` (Show Internet packets heard by radio) as in force: while false, what an iGate put on the air from the internet is left out of every topic and answer but a message or ack to our call

gate.description: `igate/gate` (Send what I hear) as in force: what the radios hear is put on APRS-IS while `state` is `connected`

state.description: `off`: both ticks are off; `connecting`: not logged in (yet, or again after a loss, or waiting for what `reason` says is missing); `connected`: logged in and verified, packets are gated; `listening`: logged in without a passcode (`gate` is off), so that nothing is gated and the stations of the internet are read only; `unverified`: the server did not accept the passcode, nothing is gated (the connection reads, as `listening` does) and the login is not tried again with another until the settings change

server.description: the name the server gave at the login (`T2FINLAND`); empty until it has answered

reason.description: why it is not connected, as a code the page says in its words (the log has the connection's own): `no_server` no server is set; `no_call` our call is not set or is none; `unreachable` the server cannot be reached; `offline` the server's name cannot be looked up (no connection); `not_server` it answered as no APRS-IS server, or not in time; `lost` the connection ended; `unverified` the server did not accept the password; empty while `connected`, `listening` and `off`

gated.description: packets put on APRS-IS since the daemon started

dropped.description: packets heard and not put on APRS-IS since the daemon started, by the reason: `tcpip` (TCPIP or TCPXX in the path), `nogate` (NOGATE or RFONLY), `query` (a generic query), `source` (the source is not a station), `own` (our own call), `duplicate` (gated in the last 30 seconds), `newline` (a CR or LF inside), `long` (more than 512 bytes), `frame` (not a UI frame, or a third-party header that is none), `offline` (heard while not connected), `not_air` (not heard on the radio: a packet from the internet or one the Dummy radio made up). A reason that has not happened is not a key

last_gated_at.description: when the latest packet was gated; null before the first

IgateState.title: IgateState

InstallInfo.description: How this copy of the daemon was installed, which is what the steps of an update depend on (neoaprs/versions.py, neoaprs/cli/installkind.py).

kind.description: `windows-installer` (the frozen program of the installer), `appimage`, `macos-app` (the Python inside NeoAPRS.app), `deb` (the Debian package, in /opt/neoaprs), `uv-tool` (`uv tool install` of the wheel, which releases before 0.16 offered), `pip` (a plain environment with the wheel) or `source` (a clone of the repository)

appimage.description: the AppImage file this runs from; empty for the other kinds

service.description: whether a service starts it: the systemd unit, the launchd agent or the Windows Run key

arch.description: the architecture of the file it was installed from: `amd64` or `arm64` for a .deb, `arm64` for the macOS app; empty for the other kinds, and for a machine the release has no file for

InstallInfo.title: InstallInfo

LayerLook.description:
With `on`, this page looks at the layer (its tick is on, the page is in front and the replay is closed: the page decides); with `on` false, or when the page closes, no more. While a page looks, the daemon
asks the layer's source and sends the page `layer_things`. Never refused: a look at a layer whose source is `none` stands and is served once a source is chosen.
LayerLook.title: LayerLookCommand

LayerReceiver.description: The own receiver's state, for its line in Settings. It says nothing of addresses or ports.

state.description: `looking` until its first answer or connection; `receiving` after an answer in the expected form (AIS: from the first AIS sentence of a connection); `no_answer` after a failure, a wrong answer or a lost connection; `connected` (AIS only) the connection is made and nothing has come yet (a receiver with no ship in range is silent); `no_ais` (AIS only) the source sent something that is not AIS first, or ended the connection without an AIS sentence

things.description: what it gave with a position at its last answer (aircraft), or the ships held now (AIS)

heard_at.description: its last answer in the expected form (AIS: the last sentence decoded); null before one

LayerReceiver.title: LayerReceiver

LayerThing.description: An aircraft or a ship, as its source tells it. Every field is always there; one that is not the layer's is empty or null.

id.description: an aircraft's ICAO address as the source gives it, lower case (it may begin with `~`); a ship's MMSI

heading_deg.description: where the mark points; null: no direction (drawn as a diamond)

name.description: an aircraft's flight, a ship's name; empty when none

emergency.description: an aircraft that says it is in an emergency (or squawks 7500, 7600 or 7700)

vertical_ms.description: an aircraft's vertical speed in metres a second, above zero climbing; null when not told (a ship's is null)

registration.description: an aircraft's registration (`OH-LZA`); empty when not known

type.description: an aircraft's type as the source names it; empty when not known

category.description: an aircraft's emitter category as the source gives it, upper case (`A3`, `A7`, `B1`); empty when not known

designator.description: an aircraft's ICAO type designator, upper case (`A321`, `EC35`); empty when not known

ship_type.description: a ship's AIS type of ship and cargo; null when not known

course_deg.description: a ship's course over ground, an aircraft's ground track; null when not told (a heading is not a course)

destination.description: a ship's destination as it gave it; an aircraft's: the ICAO code of the airport it is going to, upper case; empty when not known

origin.description: an aircraft's departure: the ICAO code of the airport it left, upper case; empty when not known

origin_place.description: the place of the airport `origin` names, from the table the program carries; empty when `origin` is empty or not in the table

destination_place.description: the place of the airport `destination` names, from the table the program carries; empty for a ship, and when `destination` is empty or not in the table

LayerThing.title: LayerThing

LayerThingsMsg.description:
A layer's whole table, to each page that looks at it and is not behind: at once on `layer_look`, after every answer of the source, at most every 5 s for an AIS receiver, when things grow too old, and
when the source in force changes (then with the new `source` and no things).

at.description: the daemon's time when the table was sent; the age of each thing's `at` is told by it, not by the page's clock

source.description: the source in force that the things are from

away.description: true when the last question failed or was not in the expected form, the connection is down, or there is no position to ask for; `things` keeps the last things then

trails.description: only in the first table a page gets on `layer_look`, else empty: the way each thing of `things` went in the last 30 minutes while the source was asked (it is asked on for 2 minutes after the last page stopped looking), oldest first: the last minute whole, older points at most one a minute and only where the way bends by more than 50 m

LayerThingsMsg.title: LayerThingsMessage

LayerTrail.description: The way one thing went: its id, and its places as [lon, lat, time], oldest first.
LayerTrail.title: LayerTrail

ListPorts.description:
Asks for the serial ports of the machine the daemon runs on, and the Bluetooth devices paired with it. Answered with `ports` to the page that asked. A KISS TCP port (`socket://127.0.0.1:8001`, Direwolf) is not a
port of the machine: it is typed. With `radio`, also the sound cards its modem lists while that radio's type has a modem on a sound card (Mercury, Sound card), and the proposals leave out what the other radios and
the GPS receiver hold; each row says who holds it (`held_by`). An `error` for a `radio` that is none (`radio.unknown`).

radio.description: the radio the list is for (its id): the sound cards and the proposals are its own; left out: the ports alone, with no sound card and no proposal

ListPorts.title: ListPortsCommand

LocatorValues.description: A Maidenhead locator (grid square) with the symbol that came with it, in a status report or in the status text of a Mic-E packet; the position is the centre of the square.
LocatorValues.title: LocatorValues

MapCancel.description: Ends the running job; the files it was making are removed and the maps stay as they were. An `error` when no job is running.
MapCancel.title: MapCancelCommand

MapEstimate.description:
Starts a dry run: how big the detailed map for `map/radius_km` and `map/maxzoom` round our position will be. Answered by the topic `map` (state `estimating`, then `estimate` filled in), or by an `error` when no job can start
(no position, or a job is running).
MapEstimate.title: MapEstimateCommand

MapFetch.description:
Starts making the maps: the world map first when it is not there, then the detailed map for `map/radius_km` and `map/maxzoom` round our position, from `map/source` or the latest daily build. The progress is the topic
`map`. An `error` when no job can start (no position, or a job is running).
MapFetch.title: MapFetchCommand

MapFileInfo.description: A map file in the data folder.

name.description: `basemap.pmtiles` (the detailed map) or `basemap-world.pmtiles` (the world: zoom 4 when it is the one that ships with the program, zoom 5 when the daemon made it)

bbox.description: the area it covers, [west, south, east, north] in degrees, as its header says; null for a file whose header cannot be read

max_zoom.description: the deepest zoom it has tiles for; the page draws a deeper one from these

build.description: the day (`20261022`) of the Protomaps build it was cut from; empty if not known (a file made by hand)

MapFileInfo.title: MapFileInfo

MapLayer.description: One layer of traffic in the topic `map`: where its things come from now and what the station is offered.

source.description: the source in force: the one chosen in Settings while it is offered, else `none` (nothing is asked, and the Layers box has no row)

offered.description: the sources the Settings list holds, `none` first: `fintraffic` only where the map's circle reaches its waters; `aisstream` (with the operator's own key, `map/ships_key`) everywhere

receiver.description: the own receiver's state while `source` is an own receiver (`radarcape` or `receiver`); else null

problem.description: why the service in force gives nothing, where the operator can mend it: `key_refused` AISStream did not take the key of `map/ships_key` (asked again after a longer wait, and at once when the key is saved; cleared by a connection that is taken); empty otherwise

MapLayer.title: MapLayer

MapProblem.description: Why a map job failed, as a code the page says in its words, with the values of its sentence (the log has the details).

code.description: `no_position` the station has no position; `slow` the map server was too slow; `unreachable` it could not be reached; `no_build` no daily build was found (`days`: how far back it was looked for); `too_big` the map would be bigger than it may be (`size` and `max`, in MB); `no_space` the disk is full; `failed` anything else (the log says why)

params.description: the values of the sentence, by name; empty for a code that has none

MapProblem.title: MapProblem

MapRetry.description: A download that did not move for a while is begun again: the page says "no progress: trying again (2 of 3)".
MapRetry.title: MapRetry

MapSizeEstimate.description: What a dry run said: how big the detailed map will be for the area and the zoom it was made for.

radius_km.description: the radius it was estimated for; it is stale when `map/radius_km` is another number now

maxzoom.description: the zoom it was estimated for

build.description: the day of the build it was estimated from; empty for a source that is not a daily build

MapSizeEstimate.title: MapSizeEstimate

MapState.description: The base map: the files, the area and detail the settings ask for, the size estimated, the job that is running, the ALOHA circles and the layers of traffic. The value of the topic `map`, told whole at most four times a second.

state.description: `none`: there is no detailed map. `ready`: there is one. `estimating` and `downloading`: a job is running (`step` and `percent` say how far). `error`: the last job failed and `problem` says why; the map files are as they were

step.description: what the running job is doing: looking for the latest build (`build`), making the world map (`world`) or the detailed map (`area`); empty while no job runs

percent.description: how far the step is; null when it cannot say (the build has no bar)

downloaded.description: the size so far of the file the step is making, in bytes (it grows while the download moves); null when no file is being made yet

retry.description: a download that has not moved for a while is begun again: which try this is; null when all is well

blocked.description: why no job can be started now: `no_position` the station has no position, `busy` a job is running; empty when one can

problem.description: why the last job failed; null if it did not, and while a job runs

estimate.description: the latest dry run (`map_estimate`); null before one, and after a download

box.description: the area those settings make round our position, [west, south, east, north]; null without a position

detail.description: `basemap.pmtiles`; null if it is not there

world.description: `basemap-world.pmtiles`: the data folder's own when it has one, else the one that ships with the program; null if there is neither (a base map the page cannot draw)

later.description: the detailed map was begun without being asked for (a place was set, or the setup guide said the map is wanted) and could not be fetched yet, most likely for want of a connection; it is tried again at the next start. False once a job runs or a detailed map is there

aloha.description: the ALOHA circles round our position, one for each radio that is on whose type shares a 1200 baud channel (Packet) and whose stations heard fill it, in the order of the boxes; none without a position

layers.description: the layers of traffic, the aircraft and then the ships: where each one's things come from now, what Settings offers, and an own receiver's state

MapState.title: MapState

MapWanted.description:
The setup guide went on from its Position step with the place the daemon has: the map of the area is wanted. The daemon begins making the detailed map for `map/radius_km` round our position, as `map_fetch` does (the
progress is the topic `map`), unless the detailed map that is there covers the place already or a job is running; it is never an error, and without a position nothing happens. A new place saved with `set_config` asks
the same by itself. The job is not the operator's: when it fails it is tried again at the next start of the daemon (`later` of the topic `map`), and `map_cancel` ends it.
MapWanted.title: MapWantedCommand

MessageCancel.description: Stops sending a message of ours that is still being sent; its row becomes `cancelled`. Answered by the new state of its row, or by an `error`.
MessageCancel.title: MessageCancelCommand

MessageDelete.description:
Removes a message of any kind (one of ours, one sent to us, one we only overheard) from the database, from the daemon and from every page: its row is a `del` of the topic `messages`. A message that is
still being sent is cancelled first, so that no attempt is made while it goes. Answered by the `del`, or by an `error` (no such message).
MessageDelete.title: MessageDeleteCommand

MessageRetry.description:
Sends a message of ours that failed, is unconfirmed, was rejected or was cancelled again, from the first attempt of the schedule. Answered by the new state of its row, or by an `error` (no such message, or it is
not in a state that can be sent again).
MessageRetry.title: MessageRetryCommand

MessageRow.description:
One message: one we sent or one that was sent to us. The rows are the values of the topic `messages`, keyed by `id` as text: the daemon holds every message (none leaves on its
own; a database with more than 10000 gives the latest 10000 at a start). A message that is new or changes (its state, its attempts) is a `set` of its row, one that is deleted (`message_delete`, `conversation_delete`) a `del`. The conversation a message belongs to is the other station: `from_call`
of a message that came in, `to_call` of one we sent.

id.description: the number the database gave the message; it counts up and is kept across runs of the daemon

at.description: when the message was made (sent messages) or heard (received messages)

direction.description: `in` was heard (sent to us, or overheard), `out` is one of ours

from_call.description: the sender: the packet's source for a message that came in, our call for one of ours

to_call.description: the addressee: our call for a message sent to us, the other station for one of ours, whoever it is for when overheard

msg_id.description: the message id the acknowledgement quotes (1 to 5 letters or digits); null for a message that came in without one

radio_id.description: the radio a message that came in came on, its id; null for a message of ours (its attempts say) and for one from the internet or kept before the radio was

radio_now.description: for a message of ours on its way (`sending`, `queued`), the radio its next attempt goes on: the one its first attempt went on, which it keeps until it ends unless Route changes or that radio is switched off, else the station's radio now (plan rule 3.2); null for every other message and while there is no radio it may go on. The page shows Route, the path and the radio's state of this radio

state.description: `queued`: it waits, with no attempt made, for another message of ours to the same station to be acked, rejected, failed or cancelled (one message to a station is on the air at a time; one not expected to be acked, given 1 or 2 attempts, never waits); it can be cancelled, and becomes `sending` when its turn comes; `sending`: attempts are being made; `acked`: the addressee acknowledged it; `rejected`: the addressee refused it; `failed`: no answer after the last attempt, or the reason in `failure`; `unconfirmed`: no answer after the last attempt of a message that was given 1 or 2 attempts (the station is not expected to ack; a late ack still settles it); `cancelled`: stopped by the page; `received`: it was sent to us; `overheard`: it was sent to another station and we heard it (`from_call` sent it, `to_call` is who it is for)

failure.description: why a `failed` message failed when it is not that no answer came: `too_long_for_radio`, its frame does not fit the radio it goes out on (it may have been sent before the radio changed; sent again, it is refused with `message.too_long_for_radio` while it does not fit); null for every other message, and for a failed one that had no answer

attempts.description: how many times it has been transmitted (at most `attempts_max`: 0, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 ... seconds after the first, no wait longer than 960)

attempts_max.description: how many attempts the message was given when it was sent: 4, 2 for the email gateway `EMAIL-2`, 1 for a bulletin (messages from before the count was fixed have their own, up to 10)

last_attempt_at.description: when it was transmitted last; null until the first attempt (the TNC may be away)

attempts_detail.description: for a message of ours, each attempt made (`attempts` of them, the oldest first; fewer for a message sent before the delivery chain was kept, none until the first attempt) with the hops of its path that a copy of our own message was heard back with; a hop heard is a `set` of the message's row. Empty for a message that came in

snr.description: the signal-to-noise ratio of the packet that carried it, dB: for a message that came in, its own packet's; for one of ours, the ack's (or the reject's) that settled it, null until one came; null too when that packet's radio gave none and for a message kept before readings were

rssi.description: the received strength of that packet, dBm; null as `snr` is, and for the Mercury modem, which gives none

route.description: how a message that was heard reached us (from the path of the first copy heard): `direct`, `via OH2RCH-2`, `via OH2RCH-1 → OH2RCH-3`, `via OH7JHF-1 (internet)` for a third-party packet an iGate put on the air; empty for one of ours and for one heard before this was kept

seal.description: what the message is besides text (encrypted messages, a daemon started with `--encryption`): empty for a plain message; `key` an announcement of the sender's public key (`send_key`; for one that came in, the key was taken, or is the one kept already); `key_other` an announcement that differs from the key kept for the station, not taken (`forget_station_key` first); `open` an encrypted message that was read, `text` is what it says (for one of ours, what was written); `shut` an encrypted message that cannot be read here (no key from the sender, no key of ours, or not for us), `text` is the ciphertext as it came

MessageRow.title: MessageRow

ModemState.description:
The modem program behind a radio's line, while its type is one the daemon starts a modem for (the Mercury modem, Direwolf on a sound card): the program's state, whether it keys the radio now and whether
it hears a signal.

state.description: `starting`: the program was started (or a Mercury something else runs is not yet answering on its control port); `running`: its control port answers; `waiting`: it is not running, `reason` says why

reason.description: why the modem is `waiting`, as a code the page puts in its own words in the language of the viewer (the log has the English): `not_installed` this installation carries no such program; `stopped` the program ended and is started again; `network` the program listens on the network and is not run; `no_port` no port was free for it; `not_started` the program could not be started or its configuration written; `sound_card` the program could not open its sound card (or, on Windows, find it among the devices) and was ended, another is to be chosen; `keying` the program could not open its keying device (or, on Windows, found several CM108 chips) and was ended, another way of keying is to be chosen; `keying_in_use` its keying port is in use by another program (Mercury: Windows error 5, or the device is busy) and the program was ended; it is started again after a back-off for as long as the radio is on; `keying_missing` its keying port is not there and the program was ended, started again in the same way; `ports_taken` another program listens on the KISS or control port of the modem's pair (most likely a Mercury the operator started himself): no modem is started beside it, no line connects to it, and the start is tried again after a back-off; the radio's type `mercury-own` is the one for such a Mercury; `receive_stalled` the program heard nothing (its receive side stalled) again after three restarts in an hour and is not started again until the radio is; empty unless the state is `waiting`

mode.description: the modem's mode, the same for every station of the type: `DATAC3` (Mercury), `AFSK1200` (Direwolf)

keyed.description: the modem keys the radio now: a frame is on the air (about four seconds), or the tune tone or the keying test is on

busy.description: another station's signal is on the channel and our frames wait: for 20 s at most (`BUSY_HOLD_MAX_SEC`), after which it is false while the channel stays busy, since nothing waits any more. The daemon judges it from the modem's spectrum (a signal as wide as a frame; a step in the noise or a carrier is none) while it reads that, else it is the modem's own fixed-threshold detector

test.description: `tune` while the tune tone is on (`radio_tune`), `key` during the keying test (`radio_key_test`); empty otherwise. Our frames wait while either is on

snr.description: the signal-to-noise ratio of the latest frame decoded, in dB; null before one

frames_keyed.description: how many times the radio was keyed since the modem started

max_frame.description: the longest packet the modem carries whole, in bytes (Mercury 123): a longer message is refused, a longer beacon has its comment cut; null for AX.25's own (Direwolf)

sound_card.description: the sound card the modem runs with (`mercury/sound_card`, or the daemon's choice while that is empty); empty for the system's default device

frequencies.description: the frequencies the project suggests, one to five, by band, the longest first: the list of the project's file (site/frequencies.json, asked a minute after the start and when a page sends `frequencies`), else the dial the version page names, else the built-in five; the page shows them in the Mercury radio's box as they are, with the words "suggested": they are not read from the radio

keying.description: how it keys the radio (`mercury/keying`, or the daemon's choice while that is empty): `vox`, `cm108`, `rts:PORT` or `dtr:PORT`

scope.description: the daemon reads the modem's UI interface: the spectrum scope can be shown (`radio_scope`) and the transmit gain is set live; false for a modem without the interface (the page shows no scope, and a change of the gain restarts the modem)

tx_gain_db.description: the transmit gain the modem runs with, in dB (`mercury/tx_gain_db`); the tune tone follows it

tx_peak_dbfs.description: the peak of the latest transmission (a frame, or the tune tone) in whole dBFS, as the modem says it; 0 or more clips in the sound card; null before one, and while the interface is not read

rx_level.description: the receive level as it is now, on Direwolf's own scale (0 to about 200: about 50 for most stations, under 5 too low, over 110 too high; `LIMITS.sound_card` has the zones): said every two seconds and at each packet heard; null while its Direwolf does not run, and for a modem that has none

ModemState.title: ModemState

NewMessageKey.description:
Makes a new key pair of ours in place of the old: the stations that have the old key must be sent the new one (`send_key`) before they can read us again. The fingerprint of the new key comes with the next
`status`. Answered by that `status`, or by an `error` when the key could not be kept.
NewMessageKey.title: NewMessageKeyCommand

NoteSection.description: One version's section of the changelog.

version.description: the version the section is of

text.description: the section as it is written, markdown: paragraphs, `- ` bullets, `**bold**` and `code`

NoteSection.title: NoteSection

ObjectKill.description:
Kills an object or an item of ours: the killed form is sent three times (at once, after a minute and after three) and then it is forgotten, and it leaves the map now. One that was never sent is removed at
once. Answered by the `del` of its row in `stations` (and in `own_objects` once the kill is sent, or at once), or by an `error` (no such object of ours).
ObjectKill.title: ObjectKillCommand

ObjectSet.description:
Makes an object or an item of ours, or changes the one of that name (a changed object starts its schedule again, and is sent at once, never sooner than a minute after its last packet). `name` is 1 to 9
characters for an object and 3 to 9 for an item, printable ASCII without `!`, `_`, `|` and `~` and without a blank at either end, and not our own call or the call of a station; `lat` and `lon` the position in decimal
degrees; the symbol is a table character and a code character; `comment` at most 43 characters (36 with a course or speed); `course_deg` and `speed_kmh` the course and speed, each or both or none; `path` the digipeaters, calls
separated by commas, or `DIRECT` for none at all (null or empty: `beacon/path`); `qru_group` the group of QRU it belongs to (up to 8 letters and digits, not `INFO` or `NEXT`; empty for none) and `on_request` true to send it
only to a station that asks for it, never on the schedule; `radios` the radios it goes out on (their ids). Nothing is sent while the call is not set. Answered by the `set` of its row in `own_objects` and `stations`, or by an `error` that names the reason.

radios.description: the radios it goes out on, their ids

ObjectSet.title: ObjectSetCommand

OverheardDelete.description:
Removes every message we only overheard `from_call` sending to `to_call` (the state `overheard`, that sender, that addressee: one pair of the Messages list's overheard rows) from the database in one write,
from the daemon and from every page: each message's row is a `del` of the topic `messages`. The conversations are not touched: a message we sent or one sent to us is never removed by this. Answered by the
`del`s, or by an `error` (no overheard message of that pair).
OverheardDelete.title: OverheardDeleteCommand

OwnBulletinRow.description:
One bulletin, announcement or group bulletin of ours: its text and where its schedule stands. The rows are the values of the topic `own_bulletins`, keyed by `slot` (`BLN1`): a bulletin that is posted, and
each time it is sent, is a `set` of its row, one that is deleted (`bulletin_unpost`) a `del`. One whose schedule is over stays, with a null `next_at`, until it is deleted.

group.description: the group of a group bulletin (`HAMS`); empty for any other

hours.description: how long it is sent after its first packet, in hours: 1, 2, 4, 8 or 12 for a bulletin and a group bulletin, 24, 72 or 168 for an announcement

last_sent_at.description: when it was last sent; null while it has not been sent

next_at.description: when it is sent next; null when its schedule is over (a bulletin: now, after 2 and 6 minutes, then every 20 minutes, 30 while a radio it goes out on is Mercury or LoRa; an announcement: the same early, then every hour; either until `hours` after the first); a repeat after the radio's random pause, which is never longer than the wait nor past the end

radios.description: the radios it is set to go out on (Send on), their ids, ascending, one at least, kept also while off; the radios it goes on now are those of them that are on and can send (with one radio that can send, that one; with none of them on, none)

OwnBulletinRow.title: OwnBulletinRow

OwnObjectRow.description:
One object or item of ours: what we send and where its schedule stands. The rows are the values of the topic `own_objects`, keyed by `name`: an object that is made or changed, and each time it is sent,
is a `set` of its row, one that is gone (the kill was sent three times, or another station took the name over) a `del`. A live object is also a row of the topic `stations` with `own` true, which is what the
map shows; a killed one leaves that topic at once and stays here, as `killing`, until its kill has been sent.

name.description: the name of the object (1 to 9 characters) or of the item (3 to 9), as it is sent: case-sensitive

comment.description: at most 43 characters, 36 when it follows a course and speed

course_deg.description: the course in degrees from north (0 to 359); null for none

speed_kmh.description: the speed in km/h; null for none

path.description: the digipeaters it goes by, calls separated by commas, or `DIRECT` for none at all; null: the path of the setting `beacon/path` is used

qru_group.description: the group of QRU (1 to 8 upper-case letters and digits) a station that asks the addressee `QRU` for it is answered with this object in; empty for none

on_request.description: true: it is never sent on the decay schedule, only to a station that asks for it (`?APRSO`, or its QRU group); false: it is sent on the schedule

radios.description: the radios it is set to go out on (Send on), their ids, ascending, one at least, kept also while off; the radios it goes on now are those of them that are on and can send (with one radio that can send, that one; with none of them on, none)

state.description: `live`: it is being sent on the decay schedule; `killing`: it was killed and its killed form is being sent (three times), then it is forgotten

updated_at.description: when it was last changed or killed

sent.description: how often it was sent since it was last changed or killed

last_sent_at.description: when it was last sent; null while it has not been sent (the call is not set, or the radio is away)

next_at.description: when it is sent next: 1, 2, 4 ... minutes after the slot of the last packet, never more than the net cycle time of its path apart (30 minutes on Mercury and LoRa: the radio's floor), plus the radio's random pause, which is never longer than the wait; a time that has passed means it waits for the radio or for the call; null for one that is `on_request`

OwnObjectRow.title: OwnObjectRow

PacketHistory.description:
Asks how many packets were heard (not sent by us) in each of the last `hours` hours: all of them, or those of one station (`call`). Answered with a `packet_history` message to the page that asked, or an
`error` for hours out of range or a call that is empty; a station with no packets is answered with every count 0.

hours.description: how far back to go: 24 for a day, 168 for a week

call.description: only the packets whose sender (the source of the frame heard) is this station, as the `stations` topic has it; absent or null for every packet heard

PacketHistory.title: PacketHistoryCommand

PacketHistoryMsg.description:
The packets heard by the hour, the answer to `packet_history`: a count for each whole hour of the clock from `start`, the oldest first, as many as were asked for; the last is the hour that is running, so
it counts what has come since the top of the hour.

call.description: the station asked about, null for every packet heard: a page that asked for several stations and for all of them tells the answers apart by it

start.description: the top of the first hour counted, UTC

counts.description: the packets heard in each hour from `start`, the oldest first (an hour with none is 0)

PacketHistoryMsg.title: PacketHistoryMessage

PacketRow.description:
One packet heard or sent. The rows are the values of the topic `packets`, keyed by `id` as text: the daemon holds the latest 200, a packet that comes is a `set` and the one that falls out of the
200 a `del`. The page shows them newest first (the highest id).

id.description: counts up in the order the packets came in this run of the daemon; not kept in the database

direction.description: heard on the air, or sent by us

source.description: who sent the frame we heard; for a third-party packet the iGate (see `gate`); for a packet from the internet the station that sent it

sender.description: the station the packet is from: `source`, or for a third-party packet the source of the packet inside it

path.description: the digipeaters, the one that repeated it marked with `*`; for a packet from the internet everything between the destination and the colon of the line (`TCPIP*`, the q-construct `qAC`, the server `T2FINLAND`)

kind.description: a telemetry report is `other`; its `decoded.type` is `telemetry`

route.description: how a packet that was heard on the radio reached us: `direct`, `via OH2RCH-2`, `via ? → OH2RCH-2`, `via OH7JHF-1 (internet)` for a third-party packet; empty for a packet of ours and for one from the internet

radio_id.description: the radio the packet came on or went out on, its id (a row of the topic `radios`, a removed one too); null for a packet from the internet

snr.description: the signal-to-noise ratio the radio measured of the frame, dB, tied to the frame where it was read (the Mercury modem and the Dummy Mercury radio give it); null for a packet of ours, one from the internet and one of a radio that gives none (a KISS TNC)

rssi.description: the received strength the radio measured of the frame, dBm; null as `snr` is, and for the Mercury modem, which gives none

via.description: the channel the packet came by, set once where it was made: `rf` heard on the radio (direct or by digipeaters; every packet of ours too), `rf-gated` heard on the radio as a third-party packet that an iGate put on the air, `is` received from APRS-IS over the internet (never on the air), `dummy` made up by the Dummy radio (it works as `rf` does and never goes to the internet)

gate.description: the iGate, for a third-party packet (`via` is `rf-gated`): `source` and `path` are those of the frame we heard (the iGate's), `decoded` is the packet inside it; empty for any other packet

tnc2.description: the packet as a line of TNC2 monitor text

PacketRow.title: PacketRow

PacketStats.description:
Asks for what the statistics card counts from the packet log: the packets heard by the hour by radio, what went out on each radio, the packets that came by several ways and the copies sent and gated
in the last hour. Answered with a `packet_stats` message to the page that asked.
PacketStats.title: PacketStatsCommand

PacketStatsMsg.description:
The answer to `packet_stats`. The packets heard (not sent by us; none from APRS-IS while `igate/enabled` is off) by the hour of the clock over the week the log keeps, or since its oldest packet when that is
younger, for each radio and the internet that heard any, the running hour last; what went out and the packets heard more than once over the last 24 hours; the copies of the last 60 minutes. Hours that
are over are counted once; the answer is at most a minute behind.

start.description: the top of the first hour counted, UTC

hours.description: how many hours each list of `heard` has: from `start` to the running one

heard.description: by radio, in the order of their ids, the internet last; one that heard nothing in the span is left out

sent.description: by radio, in the order of their ids; one that sent nothing in the last 24 hours is left out

packets.description: the packets the radios heard in the last 24 hours, a packet heard by several ways counted once (the same source, destination and information field within a minute of the clock)

frames.description: the frames those packets came in: `frames` less `packets` is how many came again by another way

repeated_hour.description: the copies the digipeater sent in the last 60 minutes

gated_hour.description: the packets the iGate put on APRS-IS in the last 60 minutes; null while `igate/gate` (Send what I hear) is off

PacketStatsMsg.title: PacketStatsMessage

PageError.description:
An error that happened in the page itself (the browser's script, not a refusal of the daemon): the daemon writes it to its log as a warning, `page error (vue) on page BUILD: MESSAGE | FIRST LINE OF THE STACK`, and keeps the latest 100 for
the support bundle. At most 20 of a connection are logged in a minute; the rest are counted in one line. No answer: a page that cannot report must not fail twice.

stack.description: where it happened, as the browser gives it; empty for none

source.description: who caught it: `vue` (the component framework's error handler), `window` (an uncaught error of the window), `promise` (a promise nobody caught)

at.description: when it happened, by the page's clock

build.description: the build of the page that reported it (the `page` of `hello`)

PageError.title: PageErrorCommand

PassStats.description: What the pairs of radios passed onto this radio from one other radio since the daemon started.

heard_on.description: the radio the packets were heard on, by its id

sent_at.description: when the latest of them went out; null for none yet

held.description: frames left unsent by this radio's limits: the burst on a fast radio; the budget, its share for packets other than messages and acks, a station's share of messages, the 30-minute floor, a frame already waiting, or a keyed or busy channel past 30 s on a slow one

too_long.description: frames left unsent because they are longer than this radio carries

PassStats.title: PassStats

PatchMsg.description:
What changed in a topic: apply the ops in order; the copy is then at `rev`. An op says what the item is, not what to add, so an op that is applied twice ends where it should. Changes are told
on a tick of 100 ms (a radio's row in `radios` at most four times a second): what changed between two ticks is one patch for a topic, with at most one op for each key.

rev.description: how many changes the topic has had since the daemon started

PatchMsg.title: PatchMessage

PhgValues.description: A station's power, antenna height above average terrain, antenna gain and directivity (`PHG5132`), and the radio range that the formula of the APRS specification gives them.

direction_deg.description: the direction of the best gain, degrees from north; null for an omni antenna

PhgValues.title: PhgValues
