PortRow.description: A serial port the system lists, or a Bluetooth device paired with it (Linux; on Windows a paired Bluetooth serial port is a COM port of the system's list). Nothing was opened or connected to find it.

device.description: the name to give as `serial/port`: `COM3`, `/dev/ttyUSB0`, `bt://AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF` for a paired Bluetooth device

description.description: what the system calls it, such as `USB Serial Port (COM3)`; `n/a` where it does not say

hwid.description: the hardware id the system gives, such as `USB VID:PID=0403:6001 SER=A1`; `n/a` where it does not say

vid.description: the USB vendor id of an adapter; null for a port that is not USB

pid.description: the USB product id of an adapter; null for a port that is not USB

held_by.description: the radio of the station that holds the port now (its id), 0 for the GPS receiver; null while none of ours does. A port another radio holds is not proposed, and the page greys it with the holder's name

usb_group.description: which USB device the port sits on together with the others of one radio (an opaque token: equal for a sound card and the serial ports on one radio's own USB hub, or on one USB device; neoaprs/usbtie.py); null where it is not known (Windows, macOS, a port that is not USB, a Bluetooth device). The page orders the keying lines by it and never shows it

PortRow.title: PortRow

ports.description: the ports, in natural order (`COM2` before `COM10`), then the paired Bluetooth devices

search.description: whether the daemon looks for the radio among the ports by itself (Linux, the ports that match `serial/pattern`); where it is false (Windows, macOS) the radio is the port in `serial/port`, so the operator picks it from this list

find.description: whether Find my radio (`find_radio`) can be asked for: on Linux, Windows and macOS

sound_cards.description: the sound cards the radio's modem lists, for a `radio` named whose type has a modem on a sound card (Mercury, Sound card) while the program is installed; empty otherwise

keying.description: the keying the daemon proposes with the card it proposes (`vox`, `cm108`, `rts:PORT` or `dtr:PORT`): the page preselects it and stores it as the radio's `keying` while that is empty; empty when no sound card is listed

radio.description: the radio the list was asked for (`radio` of `list_ports`: the sound cards and the proposals are its own); null for a list that named none. The ports are the machine's, the same whoever asked

PositionFields.description: A position as the parser made it: decimal degrees, south and west negative, speed in km/h, altitude in metres.

anyOf.description: UTC, ISO 8601 with a Z, with fractions of a second

timestamp.description: the time the packet itself carries, when it has one

ambiguity.description: how many digits of the position were blanked out, 0 to 4

weather.description: the weather a station with the weather symbol (`_`) sent after its position; the rest of the text is the `comment`

extensions.description: the PHG, RNG, DFS, DF bearing or area data after the symbol of an uncompressed position; null when there was none

timestamp_local.description: the `timestamp` was sent in the sender's local time (`/`): it is the time as it was sent, not UTC

locator.description: the Maidenhead locator in the status text of a Mic-E packet; null for any other position

telemetry.description: the base-91 telemetry `|ss11|` the comment carried (APRS 1.2), taken out of the `comment`; null when there was none

frequency.description: the local information the comment began with (`145.775MHz T100 -060 R40k`), or the name of a frequency object with the fields of its comment, taken out of the `comment`; null when there was none

storm.description: the storm data the comment of a position with the symbol `@` began with (`/HC/150^200/0980>090&030%040`), taken out of the `comment`; null when there was none

sign.description: the characters of a signpost (symbol `\m`): `55` for a comment that began `{55}`, taken out of the `comment`; null for any other position

PositionFields.title: PositionFields

PositionHistory.description: Asks where the stations were in the last `hours` hours, for the replay of the map. Answered with a `position_history` message to the page that asked, or an `error` for hours out of range.

hours.description: how far back to go: the replay offers 1, 3, 6, 12, 24 (the choices of the Stations tab's On map for) and 48, 72, 168 (2, 3, 7 days; the packet log keeps 7)

PositionHistory.title: PositionHistoryCommand

PositionHistoryMsg.description:
The positions of the stations over the span asked for, the answer to `position_history`, from the packet log: every position heard in it (a station's own, or the one inside a third-party packet), the
live objects and items heard by their names, and what we sent under our call (our beacons, and our objects by their names). While `igate/enabled` (Internet stations) is off, no packet that came from
APRS-IS is in it, whenever it was received: what was heard on the radio only, an iGate's third-party packets too, as the stations topic shows then. A station's points are thinned, the more the longer the span (REPLAY_THINNING
of neoaprs/web/views.py): up to a day, a point less than 10 m from the point kept before it or less than 30 s after it is left out; up to three days, 200 m and 2 minutes; a week, 300 m and 5 minutes.
The last point is always there, and so is the one where a station still was just before it moved off. The latest 1 000 000 position packets at most are read: on a feed busier than that, the span
begins at the first of them.

start.description: where the replay begins, UTC: `hours` hours before `end`, or the oldest packet the log keeps when that is later (a daemon that has run for less than the span, or a log busier than the packets read)

end.description: where the replay ends, UTC: when the daemon answered

stations.description: [time, lat, lon] for each position kept, the oldest first, by the station's call (an object's or item's name); a station with no position in the span is not in it

PositionHistoryMsg.title: PositionHistoryMessage

PostHours.description: The Sent for a new post of each kind starts with, in hours: the one posted last of that kind, else 4, 72 and 4.
PostHours.title: PostHours

radios.description: the radios it went on, their ids, in the order of their boxes

QruGroup.description: A group of objects a server serves near us.

name.description: the group, 1 to 8 upper-case letters and digits (`RP70`, `FOOD`)

count.description: how many objects the group has in the server's range

QruGroup.title: QruGroup

QruServer.description: A QRU server that answered, as it last said.

call.description: the server's call

groups.description: the groups it serves near us, in the order it listed them; empty when it has only sent the closing line of a group

max_objects.description: the most objects it sends for one request; null when its list did not say

range.description: the range round us it serves, in `unit`; null when its list did not say

unit.description: the unit of `range` (kilometres or miles, as the server counts); empty when the list did not say

sent.description: its last closing line as it was heard (`Sent 5 RP70 Objects Max 5@50km de DF8LS-10`); empty before one

sent_at.description: when the closing line was heard; null before one

sent_objects.description: how many objects its last closing line says it sent; null before one

request.description: the request its closing line answers, which Ask again sends once more (`TEST 150`); empty before a closing line, and when the request is not known

received.description: the names of the objects heard from the server, on a radio that request went on, since it, until `settles_at` (or the last answer, before a closing line); each is an ordinary object of the stations and the map

settles_at.description: when the counting of `received` ends, 30 seconds after the closing line (a late object may still come); null before a closing line. Fewer `received` than `sent_objects` after it means objects were lost

radio.description: the radio its latest answer came on, its id: a request of one of its groups, and one asked again, goes on it; null when the packet named none

QruServer.title: QruServer

QruState.description: The servers that answered a request for local info, and the last request. What is older than an hour is forgotten, with the daemon's restart. Told whole as it changes.

asked.description: the last request sent from here; null before one, and an hour after it

servers.description: the servers that answered in the last hour, by call

QruState.title: QruState

QueryStation.description:
Asks a station a directed query (APRS 1.0.1 chapter 15): a message to it with the text of the query, `?APRSP` (`kind` `position`: its position packet), `?APRSS` (`status`: its status report), `?APRSD` (`heard`: the stations it
hears direct, as a message), `?APRST` (`trace`: the path our query reached it by, as a message), `?WX?` (`weather`: its weather report; a general query in the specification, which many stations do not answer
when it is addressed to them) or the operator's own (`custom`, with `text`: `?APRSH OH2GBA-15`, `?PING?`). The query is sent once, without a message id: no attempts follow and no ack is expected. It is kept as a row of the topic
`messages` to the station, in state `sending` until it has been transmitted and then `unconfirmed`, whose `text` is the query; the page shows such a row (an `out` message with no `msg_id` whose text begins with `?`) as a note of what was asked. The answer is whatever the
station sends: a packet (the station's card changes) or a message (a row `in`). Not more than one query of the same text to a station in 60 seconds. Answered with an `error` when the station is not in the station book
(`station.unknown`), is no station that takes messages (`query.not_capable`: an object, an item, ourselves, a station whose position says it takes none and that never sent a message), the same query was sent less than 60 seconds ago
(`query.too_soon`) or the message is refused as `send_message` refuses it (the call is not set, the radio is silent); a `custom` text that is no query is refused as invalid.

text.description: the query of `custom`, as the operator wrote it: after the spaces at its ends are taken off it begins with `?` and has something after it, is printable ASCII without `|`, `~` or `{` and at most 67 characters, the text of a message; it is sent upper-cased. Absent or null for the other kinds

QueryStation.title: QueryStationCommand

RadioAdd.description:
Adds a radio of the type (`type`, a `key` of `RADIO_TYPES`): after the others, enabled, with the defaults of its kind, the name typed (empty or left out: none), and started at once. Answered with `radio_added` (its
id) to the page that asked, at once, and then the `set` of its row in `radios` (the topic is told at most four times a second: the row may come a few messages later, so a page that opens the new radio waits
for it), or with an `error`: `radio.unknown_type`, `radio.name_form`, `radio.name_taken`, `radio.name_label`, `setting.not_stored`.

name.description: the name typed; left out or empty: none

RadioAdd.title: RadioAddCommand

RadioAddedMsg.description: The answer to `radio_add`, to the page that asked: the id the new radio was given.
RadioAddedMsg.title: RadioAddedMessage

RadioAllowed.description: What we decided the radio's type may do (neoaprs/radiotype.py `Allowed`): a control exists only where it is true.

paths.description: our frames on it may carry digipeaters: the path controls are shown for it; false: every frame goes direct

digipeat.description: it may repeat what it hears (its own Digipeater tick, `radio/<id>/digipeat`)

smart_beacon.description: a moving station's SmartBeaconing applies on it; elsewhere the timed beacon goes with the latest fix

shared_channel.description: it is a 1200-baud shared channel: the ALOHA circle is worked out from what it hears

RadioAllowed.title: RadioAllowed

last_sent.description: when our position last went out on it; null before one

next_due.description: when the next timed beacon is due on it: its slot and the radio's random pause; null while none is planned (off, a moving station, the radio off)

interval_min.description: the interval in force on it, in minutes: `beacon/interval_min` raised to the radio's own floor; 0 while the beacon does not go out on it (off, Send on not ticked, the radio off)

problem.description: why the latest beacon due on it did not go out (`transmit.off`, `beacon.not_sent`); null after one that did

RadioCan.description: What the radio's type can do (neoaprs/radiotype.py `Can`): the controls of its box.

find.description: Find my radio (a serial line: `find_radio` with this radio)

terminal.description: its line's log can be shown (`lines`)

scope.description: the spectrum scope (`radio_scope`); whether it is shown now is the modem's `scope`

frequencies.description: the station's suggested frequencies are shown in its box

transmit.description: it can send: false for a receive-only type, which is never a message's, the beacon's, an object's, a bulletin's or the email radio, and whose line is never written to

rx_level.description: its receive level is shown in its box (its modem's `rx_level`)

RadioCan.title: RadioCan

RadioChange.description:
Changes what is given of the radio and nothing else: its `name` (empty: none), its `type` (one of its own kind), its Enable (`enabled`) or its place in the list (`position`, from 1; the others keep theirs, a tie goes by
id). Stored, then in force; the radio is restarted when its type or its Enable changed what runs. Answered by the row, or an `error`: `radio.unknown`, `radio.last_enabled` (the last radio that is on is not switched off),
`radio.name_form`, `radio.name_taken`, `radio.name_label`, `radio.type_kind`, `radio.unknown_type`, `setting.not_stored`.

radio.description: the radio's id, the `id` of its row in the topic `radios`

name.description: the new name; left out: unchanged

type.description: the new type; left out: unchanged

enabled.description: the new Enable; left out: unchanged

position.description: the new place; left out: unchanged

RadioChange.title: RadioChangeCommand

RadioChoices.description: The operator's own values of the radio where its kind has them (`radio/<id>/beacon`, `radio/<id>/status`, `radio/<id>/ask`, `radio/<id>/local_info`, `radio/<id>/path`, `radio/<id>/digipeat`), as they are in force.

beacon.description: Send on: the beacon goes out on this radio (with one radio on, it goes on that one whatever this says)

status.description: the status's Send on: the status report goes out on this radio; false by default (with one radio that can send on, on that one whatever this says; with several, while none that is on is ticked, on none); false for a radio that only receives

ask.description: Ask around's Send on: a general query (`general_query`) goes out on this radio; read as `status` is

local_info.description: Local info's Send on: the request to QRU that names no radio (`qru_ask`) goes out on this radio; read as `status` is

path.description: the digipeaters of its frames as the setting holds them (empty: the recommended path of the station's symbol, `DIRECT`: none); null for a kind that has no path

digipeat.description: its digipeater is on; null for a kind that may not repeat

RadioChoices.title: RadioChoices

RadioHold.description: A device the radio holds now in the station's table of resources: no other radio, and not the GPS receiver, is given it.

resource.description: what kind of device: a serial port, a sound card, the keying line's port, the port pair of a Mercury modem

value.description: the device as the table holds it: a serial port's resolved path (`/dev/ttyUSB0`, `COM3`), a sound card's id, the broadcast port of a Mercury pair (`8100`)

RadioHold.title: RadioHold

RadioKeyTest.description:
The keying test on the radio's modem: keys it for one second, so that the operator sees it go to transmit and come back: with next to no audio (Mercury's TUNE at its quietest level) where the keying is a
line (RTS, DTR, CM108), with the tune tone where the radio keys on audio (VOX); the radio's row says `modem.test: "key"` meanwhile. The same refusals as `radio_tune`.

radio.description: the radio's id, the `id` of its row in the topic `radios`

RadioKeyTest.title: RadioKeyTestCommand

RadioLevel.description:
The receive level of a Sound card radio as its Direwolf says it ten times a second: with `on`, this page is sent `radio_level` for that radio, the level now at once and then each change, while it shows the
level (the radio's box is in view); with `on` false, or when the page closes, no more. A page that is behind is skipped. Every page has the slower `modem.rx_level` of the radio's row. Refused, with `on`, for a
radio that is none (`radio.unknown`) and for one whose type has no receive level (`radio.no_modem`, with its `name`: `can.rx_level` of its row is false); `on` false is never refused.

radio.description: the radio's id, the `id` of its row in the topic `radios`

on.description: true starts the levels for this page, false stops them

RadioLevel.title: RadioLevelCommand

RadioLevelMsg.description: A Sound card radio's receive level as it is now, to a page that asked for it (`radio_level`): on Direwolf's own scale, as the row's `modem.rx_level`; null while its Direwolf does not run.
RadioLevelMsg.title: RadioLevelMessage

RadioLimits.description: What the radio's type cannot do (neoaprs/radiotype.py `Limits`): constants of the type.

max_frame.description: the longest AX.25 frame the radio carries whole, in bytes (Mercury: 123); null for AX.25's own

beacon_min_min.description: the shortest beacon interval the radio takes, in minutes (Packet 20, Mercury 30): the station's interval is raised to it on this radio

slow.description: a frame holds the shared channel for seconds (HF, LoRa): what the pairs pass onto the radio is limited (`LIMITS.pass` of the page)

RadioLimits.title: RadioLimits

RadioProblem.description: Why a radio, or its beacon, does not do what it is set to, as a code the page puts in its own words, with the values its sentence is made of (the English of the log is not told).

code.description: `radio.not_connected` its line is not open (`name`: the radio's name in the log); `radio.searching` the daemon looks for its port; `radio.silent` its line is open and the radio does not answer (`since`: when the latest byte came, UTC); `radio.text_lines` its line is open and the LoRa board on it sends text lines, not KISS: nothing is sent until it is set to KISS; `radio.incoming_port` its port is the computer's incoming Bluetooth port (Windows), which reaches no device (`port`); `radio.port_in_use` another program has its port; `radio.no_answer` its Bluetooth device does not answer (switched off, asleep or out of range); `radio.not_paired` its Bluetooth device is not paired with this computer; `radio.refused` its Bluetooth device refused the connection; `radio.open_failed` its Bluetooth port could not be opened for another reason (the log says Windows' words); `radio.sends_text` its line is open and the KISS device on it sends text lines (monitor text, GPS sentences, KISS written as text) and no KISS frame; `radio.write_timeout` the last write to its port timed out (`seconds`): shown until a write goes through or a byte comes; `radio.resource_held` a device it is set to use is another's (`resource`: `serial`, `sound_card`, `keying`, `modem_ports` or `gps`; `holder`: the name of the radio that holds it, `GPS` for the GPS receiver; `held_by`: its id, 0 for the GPS receiver); `modem.<reason>` its Mercury modem is not running, `reason` as `ModemState.reason` says it; `modem.receive_deaf` its Mercury modem runs and hears nothing (its receive side stalled) and is started again soon; for its beacon `transmit.off` (RX only) and `beacon.not_sent` (`why`: the code of the reason, whose sentence the page has as the refusal `error.<why>`, and that reason's values)

params.description: the values of the sentence, by name; empty for a code that has none

RadioProblem.title: RadioProblem

RadioRemove.description:
Removes the radio: it is stopped for good, and in the same write its id leaves the objects' sets, the stations' choices of it and their paths on it. Its row stays in `radios`, `removed`, so that what came by it keeps
its name. Answered by the row, or an `error`: `radio.unknown`, `radio.last_enabled` (the last radio that is on stays), `setting.not_stored`.

radio.description: the radio's id, the `id` of its row in the topic `radios`

RadioRemove.title: RadioRemoveCommand

RadioRow.description:
One radio of the station: what it is, how it is set, and how its line, its beacon and its modem are now. The rows are the values of the topic `radios`, keyed by `id` as text; a removed radio stays, marked,
so that the packets and messages that name it still have its name. A radio that is added is a `set` of its row; a change of its state, counters, lines, beacon or modem is a `set` of the row, told at most four
times a second; a change of the settings tells the topic whole.

id.description: the radio's id (an integer the database gave it, never given again): what every other row and command names it by

kind.description: the kind of radio, fixed when it was added: its tag's colour and the defaults follow it

type.description: its type, a `key` of `RADIO_TYPES` (ui/src/protocol/lists.ts), of its kind; it may change within the kind (`radio_change`)

name.description: the name the operator typed (at most 8 characters); empty for none: the page calls it by its kind and `number` (`Packet`, `Mercury 2`) in its own words

number.description: its number within its kind: 1 for the first of the kind by id among the radios not removed (`Mercury 2` is 2); a removed radio keeps its own

enabled.description: its Enable is ticked (`radio_change` with `enabled`); false for a removed radio

position.description: its place in the list of boxes (and of the radio a call no radio heard takes: the first that can send): the lowest first, then by id

removed.description: it was removed: its row stays so that what came by it keeps its name; it is no longer started, chosen or offered

dummy.description: its type is a Dummy radio: the traffic is made up and nothing goes on the air; its tag is dashed

state.description: its line: `waiting` is between two attempts to open it, or its line is open again after a write timed out and nothing has gone through or come since, `silent` the line is open and the radio does not answer (a check of the keep-alive got no byte at all in answer), nothing is sent until it does; `stopped` for a radio that is off or removed

problem.description: why it is not connected, while it is enabled and not connected; null otherwise

lines.description: the latest 100 lines of what its line saw and did, oldest first; empty for a removed radio

modem.description: its modem, while its type is one the daemon starts a modem for (Mercury, Sound card); null for every other type and for a removed radio

card.description: its sound card's own levels, read every two seconds while it runs and kept as read last while it is stopped or its card cannot be read; both null for a radio without a sound card of its own and before its card was read (`read` says which)

holds.description: the devices it holds now: a serial port, a sound card, a keying line, a Mercury port pair; empty while it holds none

RadioRow.title: RadioRow

RadioScope.description:
The scope of the radio's modem: with `on`, this page is sent the rows of its waterfall as binary frames that name the radio (*Binary frames*), first the rows kept and then the rows as they come, with `on`
false, or when the page closes, no more. Several radios can be looked at at once. Nothing comes while the radio's modem is not running or has no interface (its row's `modem.scope`). Refused, with `on`, for a radio that is none
(`radio.unknown`) and for one whose type has no scope (`radio.no_scope`, with its `name`: `can.scope` of its row is false); `on` false is never refused.

radio.description: the radio's id, the `id` of its row in the topic `radios`

on.description: true starts the rows for this page, false stops them

seconds.description: with `on`, the rows kept of the last this many seconds come first (at most the 600 kept); a page that asks again for more is sent all of them, for as many or fewer only what it lacks

RadioScope.title: RadioScopeCommand

RadioSearchMsg.description: How `find_radio` goes, to the page that asked.

state.description: `trying`: about to try `port` at `baud`; `found`: a TNC answered at `port` at `baud` and `profile` fits it, and the search is over; `cancelled`: `find_radio_cancel` ended it

port.description: the port being tried or found; empty for `cancelled`

baud.description: the speed; null for a port that has none (a Bluetooth device) and for `cancelled`

profile.description: for `found`, the key of the TNC profile (`tnc/profile`); empty otherwise

number.description: the try that is under way, from 1; 0 for `found` and `cancelled`

total.description: how many tries there are if nothing answers; 0 for `found` and `cancelled`

radio.description: the radio the search is for (its id); null for a search that named none (radio 1)

radio_type.description: for `found`, the radio type that fits the TNC (a `key` of `RADIO_TYPES`, the same as `profile` for every Packet type: 1.11's `type`, which the message's own tag takes); empty otherwise

RadioSearchMsg.title: RadioSearchMessage

RadioSent.description: What went out on one radio in the last 24 hours, by what it was.

radio.description: the radio it went out on, its id; null for what went to the internet

acks.description: our acks and rejects of messages

other.description: anything else of ours: answers to queries, telemetry

repeated.description: the digipeater's copies of other stations' packets

RadioSent.title: RadioSent

RadioStatusState.description: The status report on the radio (services/rigstatus.py `on_radio`).

last_sent.description: when our status report last went out on it; null before one

next_due.description: when the next timed report is due on it: an interval after the slot of its last, and the radio's random pause; null while none is (the status does not go on it, the beacon or the status is off, none sent on it yet)

interval_min.description: the interval in force on it, in minutes: `status/interval_min` raised to the radio's own floor (`limits.beacon_min_min` on HF and LoRa); 0 while the status does not go out on it

RadioStatusState.title: RadioStatusState

RadioTune.description:
Tune on the radio's modem: with `on`, keys the radio through its keying and sends its modem's tuning tone through its sound card for ten seconds (Mercury a steady 1000 Hz, its own TUNE; Direwolf its two tones by turns), then stops by itself; with `on` false, stops it early. The radio's row says `modem.test: "tune"`
meanwhile. Answered with an `error` for a radio that is none (`radio.unknown`), whose type has no modem or whose modem is not running (`radio.no_modem`, with its `name`), while the station is RX only (`transmit.off`) and
while a frame is on the air or the channel is busy (`hf.held`).

radio.description: the radio's id, the `id` of its row in the topic `radios`

on.description: true starts the tone, false stops it

RadioTune.title: RadioTuneCommand

ReachValues.description: How a station's latest packet from the internet got there, read from the q-construct of its APRS-IS path.

kind.description: `igate`: an iGate heard it on the radio and put it on the internet (`qAR`, `qAO`); `app`: it was sent from the internet by an app or a program and never was on the air (`TCPIP*`, `qAC`, `qAS`, `qAX`)

igate.description: the call of the iGate that heard it; empty for `app`

hops.description: the digipeaters that repeated it on the radio before the iGate heard it, in order (`?` for one that put no call in); empty for a packet the iGate heard direct, and for `app`

ReachValues.title: ReachValues

ReleaseNotes.description:
Asks what is new up to `version`: the newer one the update check found (what an update brings, from this version on), or this version itself (what the update the page's browser has seen brought: the notes of this
version, or with `since` of every version after that one). The changelog of the project at the tag of `version` (neoaprs/releasenotes.py), fetched once. Answered with `release_notes`.

version.description: the newer version, as `status.update.version` names it, or this one, as `hello.version` names it; another is answered with no sections

since.description: the sections of the versions newer than this one; empty: this version for the newer one, and for this one its own section alone

ReleaseNotes.title: ReleaseNotesCommand

ReleaseNotesMsg.description: The answer to `release_notes`: the sections of the versions asked for, the newest first; none with `problem` saying why (the notes could not be fetched, or the version is neither the newer one known nor this one).

since.description: the `since` asked for, empty when there was none

problem.description: why there are no sections, as a code: `unreachable` the notes could not be fetched, `unknown_version` the version is neither the newer one known nor this one; empty when there are

ReleaseNotesMsg.title: ReleaseNotesMessage

ReplaceOp.description: The whole value of the topic is `value`.
ReplaceOp.title: ReplaceOp

RouteMarkValues.description: One route a packet of a station came by, which the map draws (a line, or none for `app` and for a packet heard direct).

kind.description: `rf`: heard on the radio, direct when `hops` is empty; `gated`: heard on the radio as a third-party packet that the iGate `gate` put on the air, `hops` the digipeaters that repeated the iGate's frame; `igate`: heard on the radio by the iGate `gate`, which put it on the internet, `hops` the digipeaters before it; `app`: sent from the internet, never on the air

hops.description: the digipeaters in order, `?` for one that put no call in

gate.description: the iGate of `gated` and `igate`; empty for the others

lat.description: where the station was when the packet was heard (the position it reported, else the one it had before); null when that is not known: the map takes its position now

RouteMarkValues.title: RouteMarkValues

SatelliteCard.description: A satellite whose card the page has open. A frequency, mode or path is there only where the project's list marks it sure.

path.description: the digipeater path to put in a packet (`ARISS`); empty when the list has none it is sure of

footprint_km.description: the radius on the ground of the circle from which it is above the horizon

track.description: the points under it for one orbit ahead, every minute

next_pass.description: null without the station's position or with no pass within a day

looks.description: empty unless it is up now

SatelliteCard.title: SatelliteCard

SatelliteLook.description:
With `on`, this page shows the satellites layer (its tick is on, the page is in front and the replay is closed: the page decides) and has the cards of `cards` open; sent again whenever the cards change.
With `on` false, or when the page closes, no more. While a page looks, the daemon tells it `satellites` every 30 s and at once on this command.
SatelliteLook.title: SatelliteLookCommand

SatelliteLookNow.description: While the satellite is up: its elevation and the Doppler at a time, every 5 s for 90 s; the page tells now between them.

down_hz.description: the shift heard on each downlink, in their order

up_hz.description: the offset to send by on each uplink, in their order

SatelliteLookNow.title: SatelliteLookNow

SatelliteMark.description: A satellite on the map: the points under it from 30 s ago to 5 minutes ahead, every 30 s; the page moves the mark between them.

name.description: its name as the project's list has it (`ISS`, `SONATE-2`)

SatelliteMark.title: SatelliteMark

SatellitePass.description: The pass under way or the next one whose highest point is 10 degrees or more, within a day.
SatellitePass.title: SatellitePass

SatellitePoint.description: Where the point under the satellite is at a time.
SatellitePoint.title: SatellitePoint

SatelliteTune.description: A frequency of the list, and where to tune at the next pass: a downlink to hear, an uplink to send on.

rise_hz.description: at the rise; null without a pass

max_hz.description: at the highest point; null without a pass

set_hz.description: at the set; null without a pass

SatelliteTune.title: SatelliteTune

SatellitesMsg.description: The satellites layer of now, to each page that looks: every satellite shown (elements no older than 14 days) and the cards that page has open. Empty before the project's file has come.

elements_at.description: when the project's server took the orbital elements; null before a file

SatellitesMsg.title: SatellitesMessage

Saved.description: The answer to a `set_config` that carried an `id`, sent to the page that asked once the settings are in force.
Saved.title: SavedMessage

SendKey.description:
Sends our public key to a station as an ordinary message (`seal` `key`), so that it can encrypt to us; our key pair is made the first time it is needed. Nothing is ever announced by itself: a station that is to read our
locked messages gets our key this way, by hand, and we read its when it has sent its key the same way. Refused while the daemon was started without `--encryption` (`lock.off`). Answered as `send_message` is.
SendKey.title: SendKeyCommand

SendMessage.description:
Sends a message to a station: the addressee is a call with an optional SSID, the text at most 67 bytes of UTF-8 without `|`, `~`, `{` or a control character. The message is kept and transmitted at
once with the next message id; it arrives as a new row of the topic `messages` (state `sending`) and as the `out` packet, and its row changes when the acknowledgement comes or the attempts run out. It is transmitted at most 4 times, 2 for `EMAIL-2`.
When the TNC is not connected the message is kept and its first attempt waits for the radio. Answered with an `error` that names the reason when the addressee or the text is refused.

locked.description: true encrypts the message with the key shared with the station (its `seal` is `open`): the text may be UTF-8, at most 34 bytes. Refused while the daemon was started without `--encryption` (`lock.off`), while the station has not announced its key (`lock.no_key`), and when the text is over 34 bytes (`lock.too_long`)

SendMessage.title: SendMessageCommand

SetConfig.description:
Changes settings. Every key and value is checked before anything is stored: the first that is wrong is answered with an `error` that names the key, and nothing changes. A key that is
left out keeps its value. The answer to a request that carries an `id` is `saved` with that `id`, once the settings are in force (the `config` topic is told again too, to every page), or an `error` that carries it; a request without an `id` is answered by the topic alone. `web/port` and `web/allowed_hosts` are read at the daemon's start, `web/network` (and with it the access key `web/key`) and `web/https` count at once, `station/*` move our own station on the
map. A radio's own setting is `radio/<id>/<key>` (a key of `radio_values`): it is checked by the field of its kind, stored with the rest in one write and restarts that radio
alone where its driver says so; a radio that is none or removed is refused with `radio.unknown` (a removed one with its `name` and `removed` 1), a key its kind has not with `radio.no_setting` (its `name` and id,
`radio`), `email/radio` changed to name no radio with `radio.unknown`, a device another radio holds or is set to, or the GPS receiver holds, with `radio.resource_held` (`resource`, `holder`, and the holder's
id `held_by`, 0 for the GPS receiver), and the last radio that is on switched off with `radio.last_enabled` (the radio's id, `radio`), each with the key. A key of a radio's setting that does not name the
radio (`serial/port`, `hf/enabled`) is refused with `setting.unknown`: the radio's own key is `radio/<id>/<key>`, its type and Enable are `radio_change`'s. A page of another device is refused with `setting.local_only` for `messages/alert_command`, `update/url`, `map/source` and `web/allowed_hosts`.

values.description: key to the new text of the value; the text is checked and written the way the daemon writes it (`oh2gba` becomes `OH2GBA`)

id.description: the page's own number for this request, which the answer (`saved`, or an `error`) carries back; left out, the page is answered by the topic `config` alone

SetConfig.title: SetConfigCommand

SetOp.description: The item at `key` is `value` (the whole item, new or changed).

key.description: the key of an item of a keyed topic: a station's call, a packet's id as text

SetOp.title: SetOp

SetStationAlert.description:
Sets when the operator is told about a station (see `AlertWhen`): `on_air`, `within_km` (1 to 1000, null for none) and `direct`, any of them at once; all off takes the alert away. Our own station and our own objects and items
are refused. Answered by the `set` of the station's entry in the topic `station_prefs` (its path and RF only are whatever they were), or by its `del` when nothing else is set and the alert is taken away, or by an `error`.
SetStationAlert.title: SetStationAlertCommand

SetStationPath.description:
Gives a station a path of its own: the digipeaters that a message to it, and the ack of a message from it, go by way of. `path` is up to 8 digipeater calls separated by commas, checked as the setting
`beacon/path` is, or `DIRECT` for a path of its own with no digipeaters at all; an empty `path` is no path of its own, as `clear_station_path` makes it. Answered by the `set` of the station's entry in the topic `station_prefs`
(its `rf_only` is whatever it was), or by an `error` that names the reason.

radio.description: the radio the path is for (plan rule 3.3: a path belongs to the radio it was set on), its id; left out: radio 1, whose path is the entry's `path`; another radio's is the station's row's `paths`

SetStationPath.title: SetStationPathCommand

SetStationRfOnly.description:
Makes everything we send to a station RF only, or not: `RFONLY` is added as the last element of the path of each message and attempt, each ack and each answer to a query (a path that holds `RFONLY` or `NOGATE`
already gets no second one). A path that would be more than 8 elements with it is refused when a message is sent ("path too long for RF only"). The email gateway `EMAIL-2` is on the internet and is refused. Answered by the `set`
of the station's entry in the topic `station_prefs` (its other parts are whatever they were), or by the `del` of the entry when `on` is false and nothing else is set, or by an `error` that names the reason.
SetStationRfOnly.title: SetStationRfOnlyCommand

SignalSeries.description:
Asks for the readings of a station's signal in the last `hours` hours: the SNR and the RSSI its radio measured of each packet heard direct from it (`snr` and `rssi` of a packet). Answered with a `signal_series`
message to the page that asked, or an `error` for a call that is empty or hours out of range; a station heard on no radio that measures is answered with no points.

call.description: the station, as the `stations` topic has it: its packets are those whose source it is

hours.description: how far back to go: 24 for a day

SignalSeries.title: SignalSeriesCommand

SignalSeriesMsg.description:
The readings of one station's signal, the answer to `signal_series`: one point for each packet heard direct from it in the span that carried a reading, the oldest first, the latest 1000 at most. A digipeater's copy
and a third-party packet are left out: their frame is another station's signal.

call.description: the station asked about: a page with several cards open tells the answers apart by it

points.description: [time, snr_db, rssi_dbm] for each packet with a reading, the oldest first; a reading the radio does not give is null (Mercury gives the SNR alone)

SignalSeriesMsg.title: SignalSeriesMessage

SkedDelete.description:
Deletes a sked that this installation posted, by its id: the server takes it off the board for everybody. A sked that is not ours (another installation posted it, or the data folder is another one) is only dropped from `ours`: nothing is said, and the
board is read again. An `error` (`sked.unreachable`) when the project's server could not be reached. The topic `skeds` tells the new board.
SkedDelete.title: SkedDeleteCommand

SkedFrequency.description: A dial the project suggests for the HF radio.

dial.description: the dial with its mode, `7.0541 MHz USB`

SkedFrequency.title: SkedFrequency

SkedPast.description: A test that has ended, as the board had it: one row for each call that was on it. Checked again by the daemon as a row of the board is; it can no longer be joined or deleted.

id.description: the sked's id, 12 lowercase hex characters

call.description: the call that was on the air, upper case without an SSID of 0

from.description: when it began (the field is called `from` on the wire)

to.description: when it ended, after `from` by 24 hours at most: the planned end, or when its poster deleted it while it ran

dial.description: the dial with its mode, `7.0541 MHz USB`

note.description: the short note, may be empty; the page shows it as text

SkedPast.title: SkedPast

SkedPost.description:
Posts a sked of ours on the board of the project's server: our call (the setting `station/call`), `from` and `to` in UTC (`to` after `from` by 24 hours at most, not past, `from` not more than 30 days ahead), a `dial` in the form of the HF
box and a `note` of at most 80 characters (control and invisible characters are made spaces). It goes only on this command, and carries the call, the two times, the dial, the note and this installation's secret token. Answered by the topic `skeds`, whose
rows then have it with `ours` true. An `error` when no call is set (the interlock's reason; RX only does not matter, nothing is sent by radio), the sked has ended (`sked.past`) or begins more than 30 days ahead by the daemon's or the server's clock (`sked.far`), too many were posted from here lately (`sked.rate`), the board has no
room (`sked.full`), or the project's server could not be reached or would not take it (`sked.unreachable`). A board that is closed to the call is no error: the state of the topic says `closed`.

from.description: UTC, ISO 8601 with a Z; the field is called `from` on the wire

note.description: at most 80 characters once cleaned; empty for none

SkedPost.title: SkedPostCommand

SkedRow.description: A sked on the board: a call on the air at a dial from one instant to another. Every row was checked again by the daemon; the note is one line of at most 80 characters of letters, digits, punctuation and plain spaces.

id.description: the sked's id, 12 lowercase hex characters, which `sked_delete` names

call.description: the call that will be on the air, upper case without an SSID of 0 (`OH2GBA`, `OH2GBA-7`)

from.description: when it begins (the field is called `from` on the wire)

to.description: when it ends, after `from` by 24 hours at most; a sked that has ended by the daemon's clock is not told

dial.description: the dial with its mode, `7.0541 MHz USB`

note.description: a short note, may be empty (`Mercury, 10 W`); the page shows it as text

ours.description: this installation posted it, so `sked_delete` takes it off the board; no other row can be deleted from here

SkedRow.title: SkedRow

SkedsState.description: The sked board: where it stands, the dials the project suggests, and the skeds to come, the nearest first. The value of the topic `skeds`, told whole as it changes (a read of the board, a post, a delete, a sked that ends).

state.description: `ok`: the board was read (or has not been tried yet), and a sked may be posted. `offline`: the project's server could not be reached or its answer was not a board; `rows` are the last board known, and posting is off. `off`: the check is off (`NEOAPRS_UPDATE_CHECK=0`): nothing is read or posted, `rows` is empty. `closed`: the board is closed to new skeds (by the project, or for this call); `rows` are shown without the form

fetched_at.description: when the board was last read from the server (or when the one kept from the last run was); null before the first

frequencies.description: the dials the project suggests for a Mercury radio, one to five, the same as `modem.frequencies` of a Mercury radio's row (the tab does not depend on a radio's state)

rows.description: the skeds to come by the daemon's clock, the nearest start first; empty when there are none

past.description: the tests that have ended in the last 30 days: those the server lists (`skeds-past.json` beside the board) and the board's own that have ended by the daemon's clock since. Rows with the same `from`, `to` and `dial` are one test; the 20 newest tests by their end come first, then by their start and dial, each test's rows by id. Kept in memory only, so empty after a start until the board is read; empty when the check is off

SkedsState.title: SkedsState

SkedsWanted.description: The page shows the HF tests tab (and while it stays visible): the daemon reads the board now, unless it read it less than 15 minutes ago or the update check is off (`NEOAPRS_UPDATE_CHECK=0`). Nothing is answered; the topic `skeds` tells what came.
SkedsWanted.title: SkedsWantedCommand

SoundCardRow.description: A sound card as the Mercury HF modem lists it (`mercury -z`), for the Sound card choice of the Mercury radio type.

id.description: the name to give as `mercury/sound_card`: `plughw:CARD=CODEC,DEV=0` on Linux (by the card's name, which a reboot does not change); on Windows the card's recording device and its playing device, joined by `|` (one of them alone for a device with no partner)

name.description: what the system calls it, such as `USB Audio CODEC`

numbered.description: the same card by its number (`plughw:3,0`), as a setting made before named it; empty where the id is not by name

default.description: whether it is the system's default device, which the empty setting means

pick.description: whether it is the card the daemon proposes for the radio (the one it would choose itself, else the system's default, else the first that records and plays): the page preselects it and stores it as `mercury/sound_card` while that is empty; at most one row has it

held_by.description: the radio of the station whose modem holds the card now (its id); null while none does. A card another radio holds is never the `pick`

usb_group.description: which USB device the card sits on together with the serial ports of one radio: the `usb_group` of those ports (an opaque token); null where it is not known (Windows, macOS, a card that is not USB)

SoundCardRow.title: SoundCardRow

SpeedSeries.description:
Asks for the speeds a station reported in its positions in the last `hours` hours. Answered with a `speed_series` message to the page that asked, or an `error` for a call that is empty or hours out of
range; a station that reported no speed is answered with no points.

call.description: the station, as the `stations` topic has it: its position packets are those whose sender (the source of the frame heard) it is

hours.description: how far back to go: 24 for a day

SpeedSeries.title: SpeedSeriesCommand

SpeedSeriesMsg.description:
The speeds of one station, the answer to `speed_series`: one point for each position packet of it heard in the span that carried a speed (a course and speed after the position, a compressed position's,
a Mic-E's), the oldest first (a packet that came by two digipeaters is two points).

call.description: the station asked about: a page with several cards open tells the answers apart by it

points.description: [time, speed_kmh] for each position that had a speed, the oldest first; a station standing still that says so has 0

SpeedSeriesMsg.title: SpeedSeriesMessage

StateMsg.description: A topic as it is now: its revision and its whole `value`, which replaces what the page had. Patches for the changes made meanwhile follow.

rev.description: how many changes the topic has had since the daemon started

StateMsg.title: StateMessage

StationAlertMsg.description: An alert set on a station fired (`set_station_alert`): told to every page that is open, once. The page alerts as for a message to us (the sound, the notification, the browser tab, as its own choice says) and shows it in its toast.

call.description: the station

kind.description: what happened: it came on the air, it came within the distance, it was heard direct

at.description: when the packet that fired it was heard (for `within`, when the station's position was, or when ours moved)

km.description: for `within`, how far the station is, km with one decimal; else null

StationAlertMsg.title: StationAlertMessage

StationKey.description:
The public key a station announced, kept on first hearing. The entries are the values of the topic `station_keys`, keyed by call; a station that has not announced a key has no entry. A key heard from a station is a
`set`, `forget_station_key` a `del`.

fingerprint.description: 16 hex characters in four groups (`A1B2 C3D4 E5F6 0718`), the start of SHA-256 of the key, for the two operators to compare on voice

StationKey.title: StationKey

StationPref.description:
What the operator has set for one station, apart from what its packets say. The entries are the values of the topic `station_prefs`, keyed by call: a station with no path of its
own, and not RF only, has no entry. A command that sets or changes one part is a `set` of the whole entry, one that clears the last part a `del`.

path.description: the digipeaters that a message to the station, and the ack of a message from it, go by way of: calls separated by commas, empty for direct (no digipeaters at all); null if none is set, and the setting `beacon/path` counts

rf_only.description: true if everything sent to the station (a message and each attempt of it, an ack, the answer to a query) has `RFONLY` as the last element of its path, which iGates that honour it do not put on the internet

alert.description: when the operator is told about the station; null if no alert is set

StationPref.title: StationPref

StationRadio.description:
Chooses the radio messages to a station go out on (`radio`, or null to leave it to the daemon again: plan rule 3.2, the radio that heard it lately, a local one before HF). It holds from the next attempt on, also of a
message on its way, and across a restart; the station's row says it (`radio_choice`, and `radio_now` the radio a message takes now). A radio that is off is no choice: the station's row says null while it is. For a
station of the book it is answered by the station's row (and the `radio_now` of each message to it on its way); a call the book does not hold is chosen for too (plan rule 3.2: the choice is kept by call), with no
answer, and its station's row says it once the station is heard. The call is kept in its normal form, as a message names it (upper case, no SSID 0). Refused with an `error`: `radio.unknown` (no radio of that
id that is not removed), `radio.receive_only` (a radio of a type that only receives, with its `name`), or a `call.*` code for a text that is no call.

anyOf.description: the radio's id, the `id` of its row in the topic `radios`

StationRadio.title: StationRadioCommand

StationRow.description:
One station of the station book: who it is, where it was heard and how often. An object or an item is a row of its own, named by the object. The rows are the values of the topic `stations`
(keyed by `call`): a station heard again is a `set` of its row, a station that is forgotten or pruned (or an object that was killed) a `del`. When our own position changes in the settings every
row has a new distance and bearing, and the topic is told whole again.

call.description: the call with its SSID, or the name of the object or item

reported_by.description: who sent the report, for an object or an item; empty for a station

symbol_table.description: `/` (primary), `\` (alternate) or an overlay character 0-9, A-Z; empty until a position is heard

symbol_code.description: the character of the symbol in its table; empty until a position is heard

lat.description: decimal degrees, south negative; null until a position is heard

lon.description: decimal degrees, west negative; null until a position is heard

last_status.description: the text of the latest status report

last_comment.description: the comment of the latest position

packets.description: how many packets of this station were received, whatever the channel (`heard_rf` + `heard_rf_gated` + `heard_is` + `heard_dummy`)

heard_rf.description: how many of them were heard on the radio, direct or by digipeaters (`rf`)

heard_rf_gated.description: how many came on the radio as third-party packets: an iGate put what it heard on the internet on the air (`rf-gated`); counted, but never a route to send by

heard_is.description: how many were received from APRS-IS over the internet (`is`); they were never on the air

heard_dummy.description: how many were made up by the Dummy radio (`dummy`), the radio for trying the program with no radio; they work as the radio's do, and never go to the internet

last_rf_at.description: when a packet of the station was last heard on the radio (`rf`); null when none was

last_rf_gated_at.description: when a third-party packet of the station was last heard on the radio (`rf-gated`); null when none was

last_is_at.description: when a packet of the station was last received from the internet (`is`); null when none was

last_dummy_at.description: when a packet of the station was last made up by the Dummy radio (`dummy`); null when none was

heard.description: what each radio heard of the station, by the radio's id as text: how many packets of the air came on it and when the latest did; a radio that heard nothing of it has no entry

snr.description: the signal-to-noise ratio of the latest packet heard direct from the station whose radio measured one, dB (the Mercury modem and the Dummy Mercury radio do; a digipeater's copy and a third-party packet are another station's signal); null when none was

rssi.description: the received strength of that packet, dBm; null when its radio gave none (Mercury gives none)

signal_at.description: when that packet was heard; null until one with a reading was

position_via.description: the channel of the packet that gave its position (the latest one wins); null for a station without a position and for our own

packets_hour.description: how many of them were heard in the last hour (counted from the packets of the hour at the start and as they come; the row is told again each minute that it becomes fewer)

device.description: what the station runs, as the APRS device identification list names it ("Kenwood TH-D74", "APRSdroid"): by the destination call of its packets, or by the type code of a Mic-E packet; empty when unknown

last_path.description: the digipeaters of the latest packet heard on the radio, the one that repeated it marked with `*`: the packet the radio that heard the station last (`last_path_radio`) heard last

last_path_radio.description: the radio whose latest packet `last_path` is (the radio that heard the station last, radio 1 on a tie), its id; null for a station no radio heard. After a restart a station a Mercury radio heard last shows that radio's path, direct

last_route.description: how the latest packet heard on the radio reached us (empty for a station known from the internet only): `direct`, `via OH2RCH-2`, `via OH2RCH-1 → OH2RCH-3` (the digipeaters that repeated it, in order, `?` for one that did not put its call in)

heard_direct.description: how many packets came straight from the station (counted from the packets heard in this run and the latest 2000 the database kept)

last_direct_at.description: when a packet of the station was last heard direct (no digipeater repeated it, it was not a third-party packet), from the packets counted in `heard_direct`, on the radios that may carry a path; null for a station never heard direct

last_direct_any_at.description: when a packet of the station was last heard direct on any radio, a Mercury radio too (plan 6b: the green check, the map's ring and the "direct only" filter count any radio); null for a station never heard direct

heard_via.description: [the station we heard, packets] for each digipeater that repeated its packets, the most first; `?` stands for a hop that was an alias (WIDE1) and gave no call; the 8 most frequent routes are counted

gated.description: how many third-party packets this station put on the air that we heard (an iGate wrapping what it took from the internet in a frame of its own; counted from the packets heard in this run and the latest 2000 the database kept, and for a station that is in the book); not `heard_rf_gated`, which counts the packets of this station that some iGate put on the air

igate.description: a capabilities packet of the station said `IGATE`: it says it is an iGate

best_route.description: the route most of its packets came by, as `last_route` writes it, direct included; empty until a packet was counted

suggested_path.description: the path to send by to reach it, the best route turned round: empty for direct, `OH2RCH-2` for one hop, `OH2RCH-3,OH2RCH-1` for `via OH2RCH-1 → OH2RCH-3`, `WIDE1-1,WIDE2-1` when the best route has a hop with no call; null when no route is known (an object or item, or a station not heard since the packets were pruned)

heard_path.description: the path that has lately been heard to reach the station, which the first two attempts of a message to it go by when the operator has set no path of its own (the later ones go by `beacon/path`): empty for direct (at least 2 packets heard direct within 60 minutes), else the latest named route that at least 2 packets came by within 60 minutes, turned round, as `suggested_path` writes it (no hop without a call, no iGate, at most 3 digipeaters); null when there is none. Worked out when the row is sent, so a path that goes stale is told with the station's next row

internet_reach.description: how the latest packet of the station that came from the internet got there; null for a station none came from, and for one whose path does not say

route_marks.description: the route of the station's latest packet and the one before it that came another way (any channel, the newest first): what the map draws of its routes, and no others; empty for a station nothing is known of (our own, our objects)

weather.description: the latest weather the station sent (a position with the weather symbol, or a positionless weather report); null for a station that sent none since the weather log began (or was made from the packets kept)

weather_at.description: when `weather` was heard; null as it is

telemetry.description: the latest telemetry report of the station, scaled and named by the definitions it sent (read again from the latest packets at the start); null for a station that sent none

telemetry_at.description: when `telemetry` was heard; null as it is

locator.description: the Maidenhead locator of the station's latest status report (or Mic-E status text): where it says it is, to the square; null when it sent none

extensions.description: the PHG, RNG, DF or area data of the latest position of the station that had any (a position without them keeps the last); null while none had

frequency.description: the voice frequency the station gave last, in the comment of a position (or the name of an object) or in a status text; null when it gave none (not kept over a restart of the daemon for a station that does not send it again)

storm.description: the storm data of the latest position of a storm object; null for anything else

sign.description: what a signpost object says (`55`); null for anything else

distance_km.description: from our position, null for us and for a station without a position

bearing_deg.description: the direction from our position, degrees from north; null as the distance is

is_me.description: our own station: the row of the call in the settings, at the position in the settings

own.description: an object or an item of ours, which we send (the topic `own_objects` has its values and its schedule): the map marks it as ours and the card has Edit and Kill in place of Forget; false for any other row

can_message.description: a message can go to the station, and the card has a Message button: false for an object or an item, for our own station and for a station known only from the internet (`heard_is` > 0 and nothing on the radio: a message goes out by radio only); true for every other station, also one whose position says it takes none (`may_not_message`)

may_not_message.description: the station's latest position says it takes no messages (it began with `!` or `/`, or was a Mic-E one whose comment begins with the type code `'`) and it never sent a message or an ack: the conversation says a message may not be read there

radio_choice.description: the radio the operator chose for messages to the station (`station_radio`), its id, while that radio is enabled; null for the daemon's choice (plan rule 3.2), and while the radio chosen is off

radio_now.description: the radio a message to the station goes out on now, its id: the choice while it is in force, else the radio that heard the station most recently within six hours, a local one (Packet, LoRa) before Mercury, else the radio that heard it last, else the first radio that can send, in the order of the boxes; the email radio for the email gateway. Null for a station that takes no message and while there is no radio. A message on its way keeps its own (`radio_now` of its row). The page shows Route, the path and the radio's state of this radio

replies.description: the path a message or an ack of ours to the station goes by on each radio that carries no path (Mercury), by the radio's id as text: the gateway its latest packet there came by, then WIDE2-1 when a digipeater stood before the gateway, calls separated by commas, without RFONLY; a radio that carries a path, and one on which they go direct, has no entry

paths.description: the path the operator set for the station on each radio (`set_station_path` with `radio`), by the radio's id as text: calls separated by commas, empty for direct; a radio with none set has no entry (radio 1's is `path` of the topic `station_prefs` too)

track.description: the latest 50 positions, oldest first, as [time, lat, lon]; a new one only when the station moved more than 10 m or 5 minutes passed

StationRow.title: StationRow

StationTrack.description:
Asks for a station's track: the positions its row's `track` has, for a page that draws the trail or works out the speed of one station without reading the whole row. Answered with a `station_track` message to the
page that asked, or an `error` `station.unknown` for a call the topic `stations` has no row of (with the internet hidden, a station known only from there). The track is as the row has it when the command is answered:
a page that shows it asks again when the row changes.

call.description: the station, as the topic `stations` keys it

StationTrack.title: StationTrackCommand

StationTrackMsg.description: The track of one station, the answer to `station_track`: what its row's `track` has now.

call.description: the station asked about: a page with several cards open tells the answers apart by it

points.description: the latest 50 positions, oldest first, as [time, lat, lon]; a new one only when the station moved more than 10 m or 5 minutes passed; empty for a station that has sent no position

StationTrackMsg.title: StationTrackMessage

StationTraffic.description:
Asks for the latest packets of one station, for the station panel of the Stations tab: those it sent (its own source, or inside a third-party packet an iGate put on the air) and the messages we sent
to it (a message, an ack, a directed query). Read from the packet log, so that they reach back past the 200 of the topic `packets`; the page adds the packets that come after. While `igate/enabled` is off no packet
that came from APRS-IS is read, as the topic shows none. Answered with a `station_traffic` message to the page that asked.

call.description: the station, as the `stations` topic has it

StationTraffic.title: StationTrafficCommand

StationTrafficMsg.description: The latest packets of one station (at most 50), the answer to `station_traffic`, the newest first. A third-party packet is looked for among the latest 20000 packets of the log, where an iGate's are.

call.description: the station asked about

packets.description: the packets, as the rows of the topic `packets` but for `id`, which is the packet's number in the log here (the same packet in the topic has its own); the newest first

StationTrafficMsg.title: StationTrafficMessage

Status.description: What the daemon is, for the status bar: sent after `hello`, every 10 s, when asked (`status`), and when a packet of ours has gone out (the count of packets and the beacon's times have changed). It also says what the daemon costs the machine: the CPU share, the resident memory and the uptime.

packets.description: how many packets the database holds

stations.description: how many stations the station book holds

call.description: our own call, from the settings; empty while none is set (nothing is transmitted then)

lat.description: our own latitude, from the settings; null while none is set

lon.description: our own longitude, from the settings; null while none is set

beacon_interval_min.description: minutes between our position packets on some radio: `beacon/interval_min` as it is in force, the shortest of the radios the beacon goes out on (each raised to its own floor; each radio's own is `beacon.interval_min` of its row in `radios`); 0 is off

beacon_last_sent.description: when the latest beacon was sent on any radio, by the timer or on request; null for none since the daemon started

beacon_next_due.description: when the next timed beacon is due on any radio the beacon goes out on (each radio's own is its row's `beacon`); null while none is planned

unheard_radio.description: the radio a message to a call no radio heard goes out on (its id), and a text to an addressee that is no station (CQ, ALL, QST): the first radio that can send, in the order of the boxes. Route shows it as what Automatic gives. Null while no radio that can send is on

email_radio.description: the radio an email to the gateway goes out on (its id), of any kind: the one radio that can send; else the one chosen (`email/radio`, the select of the E-mail tab) while it is on and can send; else the first radio that can send, in the order of the boxes. Null while no radio that can send is on, and Send of an email is off

unavailable_types.description: the types of radio (keys of `RADIO_TYPES`) whose program this kind of installation does not carry (a Mac carries no Direwolf): the page does not offer them, and `radio_add` refuses them (`radio.unknown_type`)

new_object_radios.description: the radios a new object is ticked for (their ids, ascending), when `object_set` names none: with one radio that can send, that one; else those of the object saved last with radios named while one of them is on, else the first radio that can send

new_bulletin_radios.description: the radios a new bulletin goes on (their ids, ascending), when `bulletin_post` names none: as `new_object_radios`, by the bulletin posted last with radios named

new_bulletin_hours.description: how long a new post of each kind is sent for, in hours, when `bulletin_post` names no `hours`: the one posted last of that kind

station_status.description: the text of the status report last sent in this run (services/rigstatus.py); empty until one has gone

station_status_last_sent.description: when the latest status report was sent (kept over a restart); null for none yet

rig_state.description: whether the radio the status is made from answers: `on`, `off` (rigctld is away or the radio is off, nothing is sent), or `unused` while the status does not come from a radio (`status/source` is `text` or `off`)

cpu_percent.description: the daemon's CPU time (user and system) as a share of one core, in percent to a tenth, since the previous status that was at least a second before; the first counts from the start

rss_mb.description: the daemon's resident memory in megabytes, to a tenth; null where the system does not say

uptime_sec.description: seconds since the daemon started, by its clock

update.description: the latest version while it is newer than this one, from the daily update check; null when there is none or the check has not been answered

message_key.description: the fingerprint of our own key for encrypted messages (16 hex characters in four groups), made at the start of a daemon run with `--encryption`; empty while there is none (the daemon runs without the flag, or the key could not be made), which is also how the page knows the feature is not there

Status.title: StatusMessage

StatusNow.description:
Sends our status report now, with the settings as they are (from the text or from the radio, as `status/source` says), whether it changed and inside the interval; the next one of the timer
is an interval later. It goes out through the TNC, so it is not answered: it arrives as the new `packets` row with direction `out`, and `status` follows with the text. Answered with an `error` when
it could not be sent: the status is off or has no text, the radio is away, the call is not set, the TNC is not connected or the settings make no frame.
StatusNow.title: StatusNowCommand

StormValues.description: The storm data of a tropical storm, hurricane or tropical depression (APRS101, chapter 12), in metric units; null where the report did not have the field. The movement is the course and speed of the position.

storm_type.description: TS tropical storm, HC hurricane, TD tropical depression

storm_radius_km.description: the radius of tropical storm winds

gale_radius_km.description: the radius of whole gale (50 knot) winds

StormValues.title: StormValues

Subscribe.description:
Follow these topics (all are followed from the start): each is answered with `state`, then with `patch` as it changes. A topic that is followed already is sent whole again. A topic that is
not there is refused with an `error` that names it; the others in the command are not affected.
Subscribe.title: SubscribeCommand

TelemetryBit.description: One digital channel of a station's latest telemetry report.

name.description: from the station's `PARM.` message, else `B1` to `B8`

on.description: the bit has the sense that its `BITS.` message gives (1 when there is none)

TelemetryBit.title: TelemetryBit

TelemetryChannel.description: One analog channel of a station's latest telemetry report.

name.description: from the station's `PARM.` message, else `A1` to `A5`

unit.description: from its `UNIT.` message; empty when it sent none

raw.description: the value as it was sent (0 to 255)

value.description: `a*raw^2 + b*raw + c` with the coefficients of its `EQNS.` message; the raw value when it sent none

TelemetryChannel.title: TelemetryChannel

TelemetryFields.description: A telemetry report as the parser made it.

sequence.description: the sequence number; null for the `MIC` of a Mic-E unit

analog.description: the analog values as sent, 1 to 5 (APRS 1.2: any width, signed, with a decimal point)

bits.description: the digital values as a text of 0 and 1, B1 first: up to eight, empty when there were none

TopicValues.description: The value of each topic a page follows (neoaprs/web/topics.py): what `state` carries as `value`, and what `patch` replaces.

stations.description: the station book by call: a station heard again is a `set` of its row, one that is forgotten or pruned a `del`

packets.description: the latest 200 packets by id (as text): a packet is a `set`, and the one that falls out of the 200 a `del`; the highest id is the newest

radios.description: every radio of the station by id (as text), removed ones too (marked): what it is, how it is set, its line, its beacon and its modem. A radio added is a `set`; a change of its state, counters, lines, beacon or modem a `set` of its row, at most four times a second; a change of the settings or of the devices held tells it whole. No radio leaves it

config.description: the settings; told again after every save, though nothing differs: the settings form waits for it

station_prefs.description: what the operator set for each station that has anything set, by call: its own path (null where none is set), whether it is RF only and its alert. `set_station_path`, `clear_station_path`, `set_station_rf_only` and `set_station_alert` each give a `set` of the entry, or a `del` when nothing is left in it

messages.description: every message by id (as text), all of them sent with the first `state`: a message that is new or changes is a `set` of its row, one that is deleted a `del`; none leaves on its own

station_keys.description: the public key each station announced for encrypted messages, by call: the fingerprint and when it was heard. A key heard is a `set`, `forget_station_key` a `del`

bulletins.description: the message board by `sender/slot` (`OH2XYZ/BLN1`): the bulletins, announcements, group bulletins and group messages heard and not deleted; one that is new or heard again is a `set` of its row, one that is deleted (`bulletin_delete`) a `del`

own_objects.description: the objects and items of ours by name: `object_set` makes or changes one (a `set` of its row, each time it is sent too), `object_kill` ends one (its row changes to `killing`, and is a `del` once the kill has been sent); a live one is also a row of `stations`

own_bulletins.description: the bulletins, announcements and group bulletins of ours by slot (`BLN1`): `bulletin_post` posts one in a free slot (a `set` of its row, each time it is sent too), `bulletin_unpost` deletes one (a `del`)

map.description: the base map: the files, the area and detail the settings ask for, the size estimated, and the job that makes the maps, the ALOHA circle, and the layers of traffic; told whole as it changes, at most four times a second

update.description: Update now: whether this copy can update itself, and the steps of the update it is doing; told whole as it changes, at most four times a second

gps.description: the GPS receiver and the moving station's beacon: the latest fix, its state, and when the next beacon by time is due; told whole as it changes, at most once a second

igate.description: the receive-only iGate: whether it is connected to APRS-IS, the server's name, the packets gated and not gated; told whole as it changes, at most once a second

qru.description: local info (QRU): the last request sent from here and the servers that answered it, forgotten an hour after; told whole as it changes

skeds.description: the sked board (the page calls it HF tests): when people will be on the air, as the project's server keeps it, the dials the project suggests, and whether it can be reached or is closed; told whole as it changes

chat.description: the chat of the HF tests tab, as the project's server keeps it: whether it can be read and takes lines; told whole as it changes

chat_lines.description: the lines of the chat by id (as text), the newest 100 the server keeps, all of them sent with the first `state`: a line read or said is a `set` of its row, one the server no longer has a `del`. Read every 15 seconds while the daemon runs

general.description: asking around: the last general query of each kind sent from here (?APRS?, ?IGATE?, ?WX?) and the stations heard after it that had been quiet before it; told whole as it changes

message.description: a short note from the project, at most 200 characters; empty for none

UpdateInfo.title: UpdateInfo

UpdateNow.description:
Starts Update now to `version`, which must be the version the update check announced (the `update` of `status`): the daemon fetches SHA256SUMS, its signature and the file for this copy from the GitHub release of exactly that
version, checks the signature and the file's SHA-256 and installs it, and NeoAPRS restarts. The progress is the topic `update`. An `error` when this copy cannot update itself (`update.unsupported`, `update.blocked`), the version
is not the one announced (`update.not_announced`) or an update is running (`update.busy`).
UpdateNow.title: UpdateNowCommand

UpdateResultMsg.description: The answer to `update_check`: what the version page said, or why it said nothing.

outcome.description: `newer`: a newer version is out; `current`: this is the latest; `no_answer`: the page could not be reached or did not name a version

version.description: the latest version for `newer`, this version for `current`; empty for `no_answer`

reason.description: for `no_answer` why, as a code the page says in its words: `offline` the update server did not answer (is there a connection?), `bad_answer` it gave no usable answer; empty otherwise

UpdateResultMsg.title: UpdateResultMessage

UpdateState.description: Update now (neoaprs/services/selfupdate.py): whether this copy can update itself, and the steps of the update it is doing. The value of the topic `update`, told whole as it changes, at most four times a second.

supported.description: this copy can update itself (the Windows installer, an AppImage in a folder its user can write): the page offers Update now; else it shows the steps

state.description: `idle`: no update is running. `downloading`: SHA256SUMS, its signature and then the file of the release are fetched (`percent`). `verifying`: the file's SHA-256 is held to the signed SHA256SUMS. `installing`: the file is put in place. `restarting`: NeoAPRS ends and starts again as the new version (the page loses its socket and finds the new daemon). `error`: the update failed, `problem` says how

version.description: the version being installed; empty while idle

percent.description: how much of the file has come; null when the server did not say its size

downloaded.description: the bytes of the file so far

total.description: the size of the file in bytes, when the server said it

problem.description: for `error`: `download` (the file or SHA256SUMS could not be fetched), `unverified` (SHA256SUMS could not be checked: its signature could not be fetched or does not hold with the project's key for this version, or the list does not name the file once; nothing was downloaded), `checksum` (the file's SHA-256 is not the one the signed SHA256SUMS gives it: it was deleted), `install` (it could not be put in place, or the installer could not be started), `no_restart` (it was installed but NeoAPRS did not restart); empty otherwise

WeatherSeries.description:
Asks for the observations a weather station made in the last `hours` hours. Answered with a `weather_series` message to the page that asked, or an `error` for a call that is empty or hours out of range; a call with no
observations is answered with no points.

hours.description: how far back to go: 24 for a day, 168 for a week

hours.description: the hours asked for: a page that asked twice (a day, then a week) tells the answers apart by it

points.description: [time, temp_c, pressure_hpa, wind_kmh, gust_kmh, rain_1h_mm, humidity] for each observation; a value the report did not have is null
